recommendations.proposed: Hejduk (COL, RW, top-line winger, multi-year reasonable salary)
recommendations.summary: Send Belfour to Colorado for Hejduk; if this lands the 4th stays for Havlat and payroll drops $6.50M.
recommendations.rationale: GM tested this trade directly and Colorado offered Hejduk. They need a goalie and have none. Belfour at 92 base is the best rental on the market. Hejduk meets the 'locked on reasonable salary' test GM set on Feb 21.

recommendations.current: Tucker (TOR, LW, 29, $1.30M, 3 GP, not in any unit) + 4th-round pick (TOR)
recommendations.proposed: Havlat (OTT, RW, 23, 87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, $900K expiring)
recommendations.summary: Send Tucker plus the 4th to Ottawa for Havlat; addresses the team-wide scoring dip with a 23-year-old at 1.27 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa at 63 points with 11 expiring contracts cannot re-sign Havlat. Tucker is dressed 3 games and sits in no unit. The 4th is our only pick. Net salary swing minus $400K this season, both expiring in July.

recommendations.proposed: Draft pick (second-round caliber via over-80 expiring mechanic)
recommendations.summary: Move Svehla to any contender for a draft pick before March 19; recovers a pick from a player we will not re-sign and sheds $3.60M.
recommendations.rationale: The over-80 expiring mechanic converts a high-rated expiring contract into a pick. Svehla at 92 CHKG fills a playoff D-side need for the buyer. We lose nothing after July and gain draft capital to fund a second acquisition.

recommendations.summary: The Luongo/DiPetro monitoring task is closed. Luongo is on our roster at 94 with two years at $1.60M. The goalie trade window is resolved.
recommendations.rationale: GM declared goalies solved on Feb 19. Luongo arrived at 94 overall, 2 years club control, $1.60M. DiPetro at 81 overall was never a high-90s target. Nothing further to monitor.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 15+ MPG tonight against Ottawa; raised six times with no movement and his morale is the lowest young player on the roster at 86.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, 37 GP, 7.5 MPG, 15 pts. At 21 with the top potential marking on the roster, 7.5 minutes develops nobody. Ottawa is 22-30 and this is a development night per the GM's framework.

recommendations.summary: Bump Spacek to 12+ MPG tonight against Ottawa.
recommendations.rationale: 43 GP, 8.5 MPG, POTE 91 at 19. Morale 92 but trending toward the floor if minutes stay here. Ottawa is a game we can afford to develop in.

recommendations.summary: Stahle needs at least 15 more games this season; 4 in 66 at POTE 96 and age 20 is the worst development waste on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 17.8 MPG in his 4 appearances shows the staff trusts him. 16 games left is enough to get him to 20 if dressed tonight and every night we can afford it.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev is producing 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG and getting scratched; at 23 his development window is closing and he needs either a real role or a decision.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games is above fourth-line production. He should either play 12+ MPG or be acknowledged as a depth piece with no further upside to chase.

recommendations.summary: No change for Chlup, Nash, Gaborik, Klesla, Eminger, Chistov, Colaiacovo, or Upshall.
recommendations.rationale: All are getting minutes proportional to their current production and age. Chlup 38 pts on L2 at 19, Nash 33 pts on L3 at 20, Gaborik 81 pts on L1 at 23 — earned and maintained.

recommendations.summary: Chistov at 21 is going up in both rate (0.29→0.34) and minutes (9.5→14.5) across 52 games; flag him as a growing piece in next-year planning.
recommendations.rationale: Both production and usage rising simultaneously at 21 is the signature of a player growing into a role. Nobody has raised him; he deserves a spot on the off-season short list.

recommendations.summary: Spacek is at 0.31 pts/g on 5.9 MPG in 43 games; the pattern has deepened since my last four raises. Either commit real minutes or stop dressing him.
recommendations.rationale: 0.55→0.31 pts/g and 16.0→5.9 MPG is a player whose development is stalling despite being on the roster. At 19 this year is recoverable only with actual ice time.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 21 with 0.43→0.38 pts/g on 9.1→5.3 MPG across 37 games continues to waste his POTE 99 on fourth-line scraps.
recommendations.rationale: Same pattern as Spacek but one year older and higher potential. Raised since January 31 with no movement.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov's rate collapsed from 1.10 to 0.28 pts/g over 35 games at 23; his trade value is dropping fast. If he is a chip, trade him now.
recommendations.rationale: The 1.10 start was 10 games and is gone. 0.28 over 35 is the real number and any GM will see it too.

recommendations.summary: McCabe at 29 is at 0.50 pts/g across 66 games on a four-year $3M deal. He remains the loudest sell on the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: The 1.42 start in 24 games was unsustainable; 0.50 over 66 is who he is now. Four years and $3M for that is the biggest overcommitment on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Sundin (34), Mogilny (36), Roberts (38) and Svehla (36) are all aging together: rates down, minutes up. Plan the replacement block for next summer.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 1.46→0.93, Mogilny 1.62→0.79, Roberts 1.29→0.88, Svehla 0.78→0.44. All four are declining at the same time. Chlup and Chistov are trending up; Klesla and Colaiacovo are not.

recommendations.summary: No morale intervention needed tonight. The room is at 92 or above for every player except Spezza (86), and no trend is negative.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza's morale has stabilized at 86 rather than continuing to slide. Everyone else is at 96 or 99 with positive movement. No player is under his expected minutes band by enough to cause a crack before tonight.

recommendations.summary: Abid's 15.9 MPG against a 90+ expectation (65 pts, 66 GP) is the next morale risk if results dip; monitor before the next losing streak.
recommendations.rationale: Abid at 99 morale is fine today, but he is 4 minutes under what his calibre expects. The first losing streak will put pressure on that. Not urgent tonight.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle stays on K2 because no better D exists; this is a depth gap, not a misassignment.
recommendations.rationale: K2 checking mean is 73 against 86 best, with McCabe (84) and Abid (83) carrying the unit and Kaberle the weak link. But Salo is at 0.18 pts/g, Colaiacovo at 72 OVR, and Stahle has zero games. No replacement improves the unit.

recommendations.summary: Only three centers win draws above 75% equivalent (Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Richards 75); a single injury to Richards or Chlup leaves no faceoff coverage below L1.
recommendations.rationale: L3 mean faceoff 58, L4 mean 52. Bottom six centers cannot win the draw in important situations. This costs zone entries and puts us behind on the puck in defensive-zone faceoffs.

recommendations.summary: All even-strength lines are composed correctly for their intended roles; no changes needed before OTT.
recommendations.rationale: L1 and L2 are offensive lines and have the scoring (82/81 mean) and playmaking (81/80 mean) to justify it. L3 is a speed-and-stamina line (speed 83, Richards 86 stamina) with Klesla as the single checker. L4 anchors on Abid (83 checking). P1 and P2 are clearly tiered by skill.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour. Check his fatigue icon before puck drop.
recommendations.rationale: 93 OVR against Ottawa's 2.70 goals per game and 11.7% PP. He will face fewer quality chances than almost any night this season.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for Ottawa.
recommendations.rationale: Our L1/D1 combination (Sundin 90, Gaborik 97, Roberts 87 / Fischer 84, McCabe 83) is the correct answer to their top line. Fischer's 94 speed and 91 checking handle Havlat. Our L3 (86/82/81) already outscores their L3 (78/76/76) by a clear margin. Rearranging helps nobody.

recommendations.summary: Give Spacek the fourth line tonight and let him play. Their L4 is 72/72/66, the softest assignment a 19-year-old can draw.
recommendations.rationale: Per the GM's framework, a 22-30-9 opponent is a night we can afford development. Spacek at 76 OVR against Schastlivy 72, Johnson 72, Prommersberger 66 is a favorable test he should want.

recommendations.summary: McCabe off the sell list at 0.83 pts/g over 66 games; Eminger remains first cut at 0.42, Salo second at 0.30, Klesla third at 0.36.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe's Feb 12 panic window (0.33) has been absorbed into a season rate of 0.83 (55 in 66). He is still the best producer on the blue line. Eminger unchanged at 0.42 pts/g on an expiring deal. Klesla marginally down from 0.38 to 0.36 at age 22 with flat minutes.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly through March; his stored 84 TOUG and 88 CHKG are the free sixth checker this roster needs for playoff depth.
recommendations.rationale: Today's display reads him at 70/83 because engine form suppresses the whole club, but the stored grades are 84/88. At 83 displayed CHKG he already matches Svehla's 83. He is the sixth man the checking group is missing and costs nothing.

recommendations.summary: Do not spend trade currency on toughness this deadline; the 73 ceiling is a form artifact and stored grades carry six at 80+.
recommendations.rationale: The Feb 21 finding at high confidence established that stored TOUG is 80+ on six players, with the entire club reading 10-14 points depressed. Tucker at stored 84 confirms it. Chasing an external tough-guy for a gap that does not exist wastes the fourth-rounder or Tucker's own trade value.

recommendations.summary: Evaluate Salo (88 scoring, 30) in March games as playoff extra body; he is the highest-grade player not in any unit.
recommendations.rationale: Salo reads 88 on scoring and 30 years old, the same age as McCabe. He is not in any line slot. A playoff roster needs 7 D or 13 F and he is the best available bench player by grade.

recommendations.summary: Dress Koltsov (92 speed, 23) in at least half of the remaining 18 games; 92 SPEE with no evaluation plan wastes a roster spot.
recommendations.rationale: His 92 displayed speed is the second-best on the club behind Gaborik's 98. At 23 with no unit, the GM cannot grade him for next season's rotation in June if he never plays.

recommendations.summary: Build a tiered summer 2005 re-signing plan before the season ends: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Upshall on 5-6 years; Alexeev, Chistov, Colaiacovo, Abid, Smirnov on 2-3 years to split the renewal load across 2005 and 2007.
recommendations.rationale: 15 contracts worth $25.30M expire in the same July. All on 5-6 years means 10+ re-signings in July 2006 for the 2-year group (Chlup, Luongo, Klesla, Ouellet, Spezza, all POTE 95+) with no offsetting depth deals. Staggering depth onto 2-3 year terms pushes those renewals to 2007.

recommendations.summary: The age curve and payroll structure are sound: 26 players under 30, five veterans naturally rolling off within 24 months, and $24.28M profit funds the raises the young core will demand.
recommendations.rationale: 15 players at 23 or under, 11 at 24-29, only 5 at 34+. The veteran salary ($18.30M across Sundin, Mogilny, Svehla, Roberts, Belfour) expires or shrinks within two years, creating space for young-core raises without threatening profitability.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's POTE 99 and 5.3 MPG at age 21 means the club has a future top-six centre on the bench; if the plan depends on him being part of the core by 2006-07, he needs 12+ MPG now.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza has 15 points in 37 games on $1.00M with 2 years left (expires July 2006). If he is to be a cornerstone, development clock is ticking: by the time his contract is up he is 23 and still needs to prove top-six worthiness.

recommendations.summary: Decide on the Belfour-to-Colorado-for-Hejduk deal by March 10; this gates the Havlat package and recovers value from a 39-year-old who may retire.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 92 base, $6.50M expiring, and the only over-80 asset on the roster. If the deal lands, the 4th-rounder funds Havlat; if it doesn't, both upgrades are lost. GM's own Feb 21 note worries about losing him for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Havlat from Ottawa for Tucker plus the 4th-rounder once the Belfour decision is settled.
recommendations.rationale: Havlat is 23, 87 base, 80 points in 63 games, $900K expiring. OTT at 63 points with 11 expiring cannot retain him. He is the depth-scoring answer the roster lacks.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts before March 19 for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 38, $2.70M, expiring, over 80. He is not in the playoff plan at 38 and not in the future plan at all. The mechanic converts him to a pick at no hockey cost.

recommendations.summary: Offer Gaborik a 5-6 year deal at season end; he is the first priority of July.
recommendations.rationale: At 23, 91 base, POTE 90, 67 points in 45 games on $1.10M, he is the best young player on the roster. If he hits the market he will be bid up beyond what we want to pay.

recommendations.summary: Offer Eminger a 5-6 year deal at season end alongside Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: At 21, $1.20M, POTE 99, GM has explicitly protected him. Locking him long is the cheapest cornerstone we will ever sign.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on 5 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: At 27 on $1.90M, he is in his prime as our top offensive defenseman. Five years locks the position without a July bidding war.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards on 5-6 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: At 24 on $1.00M, he is our long-term centre solution. Cheap, young, already deployed at third-line centre.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash on 5 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: At 20 on $1.20M, he is the youngest of the core five. Five years now means his deal does not cluster with Gaborik or Richards in three summers.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Smirnov; clear the roster slot at season end.
recommendations.rationale: At 20, POTE 70, zero games played. The coach's read is correct: the spot is wasted. POTE 70 does not justify a roster slot over a POTE 90+ call-up.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla in the off-season via the over-80 mechanic; keep him for the playoffs.
recommendations.rationale: At 36, $3.60M, 92 CHKG stored, he is a pick-recovery asset. But gutting the top pair two weeks before the deadline weakens the playoff D-corps of a first-place team. Convert him in July instead.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Havlat (OTT, LW, 84 ovr, 82 pts/65 GP, $0.90M expiring, POTE 85, age 23) for Tucker plus the 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 63 points with 11 expiring deals cannot retain him. Fills the depth-scoring gap with a player on our timeline. Package is already identified and costs only a player not in any unit plus our single pick.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Cammalleri (LA, RW, 79 ovr, 47 pts/43 GP, POTE 97, age 22, $1.10M expiring) for Koltsov plus a recovered pick from Svehla.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 64 points with 14 expiring deals cannot re-sign him over their own cap pressure. At 22 with POTE 97 he is re-signable for five years and fills a top-six wing permanently, unlike any rental. Koltsov (92 speed, not in any unit) is the natural return piece.

recommendations.summary: Monitor ATL's re-signing binary: if they keep Heatley over Kovalchuk (86 ovr, 105 pts/62 GP, $1.10M expiring, POTE 85, age 21), he becomes available for Koltsov plus Chistov.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 64 points with 11 expiring cannot retain both. Kovalchuk is the highest-scoring available player in the league. But acquiring him costs Koltsov AND Chistov (both POTE 95+) for a rental unless we commit $3-5M at renewal on top of the $25.30M July wall. Only pursue if ATL re-signs Heatley first.

recommendations.summary: Conroy (CGY, C, 76 ovr, 77 pts/64 GP, 94 FACE, $2.00M expiring, age 31) fills the faceoff gap and adds centre production from the worst team in the league, but costs a young asset for a rental.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 50 points, 10 expiring, desperate. He closes the faceoff gap (94 FACE) and adds 77 points of centre production tonight. But at 31 and expiring he is a pure rental, and any package CGY accepts uses a POTE 95+ prospect. Recommended only if the GM values this playoff run above Chistov's future.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla ($3.60M expiring, 36, 83 CHKG) for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: At 36 with one year left he walks in July for nothing. The over-80 expiring mechanic converts him to a pick, which funds a second deadline package (Cammalleri or Komisarek) without spending the 4th already earmarked for Havlat. If he goes to a contender needing a checking D-man, they accept an aging body for a short-term boost.

recommendations.summary: Komisarek (MTL, D, 76 ovr, 70 pts/65 GP, POTE 91, age 23, $1.10M expiring) from MTL at 51 points with 15 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: MTL is the worst seller in the league with the most expiring deals. At 23 with POTE 91 and 70 points from the blue line he is a future top-pair defenceman. But this competes for the same assets as Cammalleri; the GM should choose one or the other based on whether the priority is wing depth or blue-line depth.

recommendations.summary: Send Belfour to Colorado for Hejduk now; the GM confirmed Colorado accepts this on Feb 21 and the deal is ready to execute.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 92 base with 18-3 2.27 GAA in 21 GP is exactly what a contender without a goalie needs for a Cup run. Colorado have no capable backup. We shed $6.50M, gain a top-line wing without spending the 4th-rounder, and free it for Havlat. The GM tested this trade on Feb 21 and Colorado said yes.

recommendations.proposed: Havlat (OTT, 23, 84 overall, 82 pts/65 GP, $900K expiring, POTE 85)
recommendations.summary: Send Tucker plus the 4th-rounder to Ottawa for Havlat; if rejected, add Salo ($2.60M, 2yr, not in any unit) to sweeten.
recommendations.rationale: Havlat is 82 points on $900K, 23 years old, and Ottawa at 63 points with 11 expiring deals cannot retain him. Tucker plays 3 games for us but gives Ottawa a checking wing with 2 years of team control for next season. The 4th-rounder is low value; Salo as an add clears $2.60M from our July renewal list and adds a body Ottawa can use.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla to a contender for a draft pick before March 7 so the pick is re-tradeable before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla at 83+ displayed overall with 92 CHKG and 94 ENDU is a playoff-ready shutdown pair for any contender thin at the blue line. The over-80 expiring mechanic converts him to a pick. Must close by March 7 because picks need 10 games before re-use and the deadline is March 19. We shed $3.60M with no incoming salary. If the pick arrives, it funds Komisarek (MTL, 23, POTE 90, 83 TOUG, $1.10M expiring) from a 46-point seller.

recommendations.proposed: Kovalchuk or Heatley (ATL, free agency July 2005)
recommendations.summary: If no deadline deal lands, pivot to summer free agency: ATL cannot re-sign both Kovalchuk (89 base, 105 pts) and Heatley (91 base, 96 pts), so one will be available at no trade cost.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 64 points with 11 expiring deals face the same retention math in July. We can sign one to a 5-6 year deal with no trade currency required, only salary. This is the fallback plan if the three deadline proposals all fail.

recommendations.summary: Close the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task. Luongo is our starter (94, 65 GP, 2yr deal) and DiPietro (82, 3.64 GAA) does not fit the high-90s target profile the GM set on Jan 15.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo played all 65 games and is locked for two years. DiPietro's 7-12 record and 0.849 SP in 21 games at age 23 with an expiring deal make him a low-80s backup, not the franchise goalie the GM wants from a non-contender.

recommendations.summary: Spezza must be reinstated to 12+ MPG in remaining games or traded before the deadline; his morale at 86 is now costing us a grade on every attribute.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21 with 15 points in 37 games and 7.5 MPG. He's been raised six times with no movement. His morale at 86 is now in the band that subtracts from all grades, so keeping him scratched costs on-ice quality from the player we're trying to develop.

recommendations.summary: Stahle's movement from 0 to 4 games is the right direction; keep the slow ramp.
recommendations.rationale: He earned 17.8 MPG in his 4 appearances, showing the GM trusts him when he does play. At 20 with POTE 96 the priority is continuing to dress him, not forcing him into a full role.

recommendations.current: Chlup (54 GP, 16.1 MPG, 38 pts, L2, age 19)
recommendations.summary: Chlup is earning everything he's getting; 0.70 pts/g on 16.1 MPG on the second line is exactly where he belongs.
recommendations.rationale: 38 points in 54 games at 19 on the second line with morale at 96. No intervention needed.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov at POTE 70 is not a high-ceiling waste; he is a depth forward not yet ready for this level.
recommendations.rationale: Zero games at 20 with POTE 70 is a fair outcome for a player on the edge of this roster. Not every young player is owed games.

recommendations.summary: Plan next season around Chlup as a permanent top-nine forward at 17+ MPG.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62 to 0.73 pts/g with minutes up from 11.0 to 17.7 at 19. He is climbing while carrying a heavier load, which is the signal of a real breakout.

recommendations.summary: Chistov is growing into a third-line role: minutes up from 9.5 to 14.4 with his rate improving from 0.29 to 0.32.
recommendations.rationale: He is the young option that helps the L3 stamina problem. Give him the remainder of this season at 14+ MPG to confirm.

recommendations.summary: Spacek needs a decision this week: 12+ MPG or full scratch. 6.0 MPG at 0.32 pts/g at age 19 is a year wasted.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes collapsed from 16.0 to 6.0 and his rate halved from 0.55 to 0.32. Raised four times in February with no movement. This is the biggest development failure after Spezza.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 5.3 MPG and 0.38 pts/g at 21 with POTE 99 is now a confirmed wasted year. He needs a real role next season or a roster decision.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes fell from 9.1 to 5.3 and rate from 0.43 to 0.38. Raised six times with no change in his usage.

recommendations.summary: McCabe is the loudest summer sell. 0.46 pts/g on the full window at 29, four years and $3M remaining.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate collapsed from 1.42 to 0.46. The January recovery note is dead. No defenceman playing 22 MPG for $3M should be at 0.46.

recommendations.summary: Salo at 0.17 pts/g on 14.6 MPG at age 30 is below fourth-pair production. Sell this summer.
recommendations.rationale: Rate collapsed from 0.40 to 0.17 while minutes fell from 20.3 to 14.6. Two years and $2.6M left on the contract. The cheapest meaningful cut behind McCabe.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny should not be playing 19.8 MPG at 36. Cut him to 15 or less and give those minutes to Chistov or Spacek.
recommendations.rationale: His rate halved from 1.62 to 0.81 while his minutes went up from 16.9 to 19.8. He is absorbing minutes the third line cannot carry, which is accelerating the decline.

recommendations.summary: Roberts at 38 went from 16.5 to 21.0 MPG while production fell from 1.29 to 0.85. Plan for a reduced role next season.
recommendations.rationale: Same pattern as Mogilny and Sundin: aging players absorbing minutes because L3 cannot absorb them. The trio is not sustainable at these loads.

recommendations.summary: Keep dressing Stahle for the remaining 17 games. Four games at 17.8 MPG is the start we needed at POTE 96.
recommendations.rationale: He had zero games through 49. Now at four. At 20 he needs every shift he can get before next season.

recommendations.summary: Eminger at 0.50 pts/g on the full window with minutes up from 15.0 to 17.0. His recovery is holding. Keep him in the lineup.
recommendations.rationale: Feb 19 recovery note is confirmed by the full-window trend. If he finishes above 0.50 we discuss his expiring contract. Below 0.45 the sell case returns.

recommendations.summary: The room is at 92+ across the board with the winning streak lifting everyone. No morale intervention needed tonight.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 86 is the only sub-90 and is ticking up (+1). Spacek and Alexeev surged +5 each to 92. The streak is doing the work a line change would otherwise have to do.

recommendations.summary: We need one more defenceman who checks in the 80+ range; our only two are McCabe and Fischer and they are already paired together on D1.
recommendations.rationale: D Pair 2 (Svehla, Kaberle) has no player above 83 checking -- neither appears on the role inventory. D Pair 3 (Eminger, Klesla) is young with no checking specialist either. Against quality opponents the auto-pairing sends this pair against the opponent's second line with nothing to match their skill. The gap is one 80+ checking D.

recommendations.summary: The forward lines are built correctly for their roles and no shuffle improves the unit attribute profile without breaking chemistry.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has grit and scoring, L2 has skill and faceoff from Chlup (80), L3 has depth and speed. Moving a checker to L2 means removing one from L1 or L3 and creating the same gap elsewhere.

recommendations.summary: P1 is built around possession and skill (scoring 82, playmaking 82, clutch 85) and the unit is coherent.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik at 98 scoring and 99 playmaking is the engine. Sundin provides the draw and the point shot. Roberts and McCabe screen and cycle. No change needed.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for FLA tonight. Every line matchup favours us and their best centre is out until March 19.
recommendations.rationale: FLA without Nieuwendyk (81 OVR, FACE 94) has no line that out-talents ours. Their PP is 20/199 (10.1%). We are 3-0-0 in the season series, 11-5 in goals. The existing line construction already exploits the depth gap on every pair.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour unless his fatigue icon shows tired before puck drop.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour reads 93 OVR with morale 99 tonight. FLA scores 2.90 per game but 1.67 against us this season. No reason to hand this to Ouellet (82 OVR).

recommendations.summary: McCabe's recent window is 0.20 pts/g (1 pt in 5 games since Feb 21) but season rate of 0.82 still earns top-pair minutes. No change to his role.
recommendations.rationale: 0.82 pts/g at 22.8 MPG is still our best offensive D by 0.28. The cold streak is a trajectory concern for next season's $3M x 4 deal, not a reason to move him now.

recommendations.summary: Eminger stays on the sell list: 0.43 pts/g season, 0 points in 3 since Feb 21, expiring $1.2M.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate has not recovered since Feb 19 and continues drifting down. He will be a cheap UFCA in April if we don't get something.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker on the fourth line to give it 88 TOUG and 92 CHKG without spending currency.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is in no unit with stored TOUG 88 and CHKG 92. The fourth line (Pesonen 67, Williams 67, Mowers 71) is the weakest assignment in the league per the coach. This closes the displayed toughness gap at zero cost.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla (36, 92 CHKG, $3.60M expiring) before March 19 to recover a pick before his value walks.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla's 83 displayed overall is form-depressed from his 85 base, but the key number is his $3.60M expiring salary at 36. The over-80 expiring pick-recovery mechanic applies. Eminger (21, POTE 99) is the long-term replacement.

recommendations.summary: Do not spend deadline currency on a faceoff centre; the game's faceoff mechanics are undecoded and the causal link to winning is unproven.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 90 FACE, Chlup 75, Richards 70. The gap is real on the sheet but the GM already killed Bell/Doan as wing-based fixes. No centre at 85+ FACE is available cheaply. A first or second round pick is better spent on Havlat scoring.

recommendations.summary: Salo at 81 base and 70 CHKG is healthy depth who is not dressed; keep him available for injury cover on the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: With six defencemen on the roster (Kaberle, Svehla, Salo, McCabe, Fischer, Eminger), the playoff roster will need to carry five or six. Salo's 81 overall is the most underused asset on the blue line.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour, Svehla, and Roberts before March 19 to recover draft capital via the over-80 expiring mechanic; the club owns nothing better than a 4th-rounder today.
recommendations.rationale: Combined $12.80M in expiring salaries, combined age 113, combined POTE 157. Each qualifies for the pick-recovery trade. Recovering three picks in rounds 2-3 transforms the draft-capital position for the 2005-07 windows.

recommendations.current: Gaborik, Richards, Abid, Nash, Alexeev, Upshall, Chistov, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Kaberle
recommendations.summary: Re-sign all ten expiring young-core players at summer; Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, and Chistov on 5-6 years, the remainder on 3-4.
recommendations.rationale: Ten players worth $12.50M combined in expiring deals carry POTE 75-99 and produced 339 combined points this season. Letting even three of them walk at market price after breakout years costs multiple first-round picks to replace each.

recommendations.summary: Fischer at $3.70M for four more years is the worst contract on the roster (0.46 pts/g, POTE 90 unrealized) but cannot be renegotiated; revisit as trade bait in 2006 once his overall settles.
recommendations.rationale: No mid-contract renegotiation is possible. His POTE 90 at 24 means the production could still arrive. Building trade bait around him requires knowing his ceiling, which one more season will show.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Havlat from Ottawa for Tucker plus our 4th-rounder before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Havlat is 87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, age 23, $900K expiring. Ottawa at 62 pts with 11 expiring deals cannot retain him. Tucker (29, 83 CHKG, in no unit) is a cost-free piece that helps Ottawa next season.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla before March 19 for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is 36, $3.60M, 1 year remaining, over 80 overall. Any contender needing a top-four blueliner gives a pick for rental. We do not want him at renewal age.

recommendations.summary: If GM confirms the retirement hedge, trade Belfour for a young goalie on a reasonable salary before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, age 39. GM raised the possibility on Feb 21 as a hedge against retirement. Colorado wanted him and offered Hejduk. If not traded, he walks in July and we lose a pick-recovery asset worth $6.50M in salary relief.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to 5-6 years at season end before any bidding war.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, age 23, 67 pts/45 GP pace, POTE 90, $1.10M. He is the most important contract on the roster and the cheapest star we will ever have at this price.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to 5-6 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, POTE 99, $1.20M, protected by the GM. The single highest-potential defenseman on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle to 5-6 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: Age 26, $1.90M, our top defenseman. Star length on a star contract.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to 5-6 years despite the rate decline.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged 1.08 to 0.78 ppg, but he is 24 on $1.00M. A second-line centre at a fourth-line price is worth locking before he gets expensive.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to 5-6 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M. The rate decline (0.83 to 0.46) is a concern but at 20 the cost of locking is low and the upside of a miss is a cheap depth player.

recommendations.summary: Sign Abid to 2 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: Age 24, $0.40M, 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG on stored grades. The coach's toughness target at no cost.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk at season end. Do not offer renewal.
recommendations.rationale: 38 years old, $2.70M. No path back to a useful role and the money is better spent on the young core.

recommendations.summary: Renew these five on 2 years only if they show development by April; otherwise let them walk or move at the deadline for depth.
recommendations.rationale: All five are 20-23 on $0.40-1.20M expiring deals. None are core. They are either trade bodies for the Havlat or Svehla packages or depth renewals. Decide per-player in March.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour to Colorado for Hejduk; two years of 98-point RW production at $2.50M is the single best return for Belfour available.
recommendations.rationale: Hejduk is 29, 91 base, 98 pts/62 GP, $2.50M with 2 years left. Colorado at 80 points needs a playoff goalie and Belfour at 92 base fills that. The GM floated this on Feb 21. It converts Belfour's expiring value into two years of production instead of a 4th-rounder.

recommendations.summary: If ATL re-signs Heatley, pivot to Kovalchuk: 104 pts/61 GP at 21 on $1.10M expiring from a 63-point club.
recommendations.rationale: Kovalchuk (89 base, 104 pts/61 GP, 21, $1.10M, 1yr) is the highest-production player available on any seller. ATL at 63 points with 11 expiring cannot retain both him and Heatley. At 21 he could be re-signed long-term. Package: Salo (expiring $2.50M) plus the 4th.

recommendations.summary: If ATL re-signs Kovalchuk, pivot to Heatley: 96 pts/58 GP at 24 on $1.10M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Heatley (91 base, 96 pts/58 GP, 24, $1.10M, 1yr) is the better scorer tonight. The ATL binary means we get one or the other, not both. Same package structure.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Daze from CHI: 102 pts/63 GP at 29, $3.00M expiring, for the 4th plus a depth piece.
recommendations.rationale: Daze (89 base, 102 pts/63 GP, 29, $3.00M, 1yr) from CHI at 55 points with 10 expiring deals. His 89 base qualifies for the over-80 mechanic. CHI cannot re-sign him and won't make the playoffs. He is a pure rental scorer at the cheapest 100-point price on the board.

recommendations.summary: Package: Tucker plus the 4th to OTT for Havlat; 87 base, 81 pts/64 GP at 23, $900K expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker (TOUG 88, CHKG 92) is in no unit and is free OTT would dress on a top line. Havlat at 23 with 81 points is cheaper than Daze and younger, but uses our only pick. Choose Havlat over Daze if Belfour stays; choose Daze if Hejduk comes via Belfour and the 4th must stay home.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Stuart from SJ: 87 base D, 42 pts/63 GP at 25, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring. The arrived answer at top-pair defence.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 58 points with 14 expiring deals is a seller. Stuart fills the slot Svehla (36, expiring) leaves when he goes. At 25 with POTE 91 he is the bridge between Eminger's development and the current roster. Could be re-signed at a team-friendly rate.

recommendations.summary: If the GM decides the faceoff gap matters: Conroy (94 FACE, 77 pts/64 GP, 33, $2.00M expiring) from 50-point CGY for Chistov plus the 4th.
recommendations.rationale: Conroy (85 base, 94 FACE, 77 pts/64 GP, 33, $2.00M, 1yr) is the best faceoff centre on a seller. CGY at 50 points with 10 expiring is desperate to move salary. At 33 he is a one-year rental. Only pursue if the GM overrides his Feb 25 position that faceoffs from a wing do not solve the problem.

recommendations.summary: Send Belfour to COL for Hejduk; this is the keystone deal that generates space and keeps the 4th for a second target.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 92 base expiring is our only over-80 pick-recovery asset. Getting Hejduk (2yr, $2.50M, 91 base, 98 pts) instead of a 4th is a 4x upgrade in return value. COL at 80 points needs a playoff-calibre backup. Acceptance uncertain but the GM already tested this on Feb 21.

recommendations.proposed: Hejduk (RW, 29, 91 base, 98 pts/62 GP, $2.50M, 2 yrs left)
recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour to Colorado for Hejduk straight up; the GM tried this on Feb 21 and COL were receptive.
recommendations.rationale: COL at 80 points need a playoff goalie and the GM confirmed they have none; Belfour's 18-3 2.27 GAA is exactly what they need. We shed $4.00M net and get two years of 98-point right-wing production. The 4th stays home for Havlat.

recommendations.current: Tucker (LW, 29, $1.30M, 2 yrs, in no unit, 1pt/3GP) + 4th-round pick
recommendations.summary: Send Tucker plus the 4th-rounder to Ottawa for Havlat; they cannot re-sign him at 81 points.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 62 points with 11 expiring deals must sell Havlat or lose him. Tucker's 92 CHKG and 88 TOUG give them a physical body on a controlled deal. We get a 23-year-old at $900K who could be extended cheaply. Net payroll minus $400K.

recommendations.proposed: A second or third-round draft pick from a contender with a blueline gap
recommendations.summary: Move Svehla to a contender for a pick before March 19; his 92 CHKG prices well and he walks in July otherwise.
recommendations.rationale: The over-80 expiring mechanic converts him to a pick. A contender with a D injury gets a top-pair checker for the playoff run. We shed $3.60M and recover draft capital we currently do not have. Execute only after the Belfour and Havlat moves are settled so the defense depth is already addressed.

recommendations.summary: Goalie trade window task is complete: Luongo is here (91 base, 2yrs), DiPietro has not developed (79 base unchanged across 46 GP), and the GM has closed the topic.
recommendations.rationale: DiPietro's 46-GP sample shows 23-20, 2.90 GAA but 0.872 save pct and zero movement in base overall. Luongo's arrival makes any acquisition redundant. No further monitoring needed.

recommendations.summary: Return Spezza to the lineup at 10+ MPG for a stretch of games; his morale at 86 is the lowest on the roster and his 7.5 MPG is well below any reasonable band for a 21-year-old with POTE 99.
recommendations.rationale: 7.5 MPG in 37 games at POTE 99 has produced 15 points and a morale reading 6 points below the next-worst young player. The rotation that keeps Spacek and Koltsov cycling is fine for players with different ceilings, but Spezza's scouting grade puts him above it.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle at least every third game over the remaining 18; 4 appearances in 64 is not a development plan at POTE 96 and age 20.
recommendations.rationale: He showed 17.8 MPG in his four chances, so the coaching staff clearly trusts him when he suits up. He just isn't suiting up.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov at POTE 70 and 0 games at 20 does not justify a roster spot in the development rotation; either dress him to evaluate or clear the slot.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's rotation philosophy is about developing high-ceiling young players. POTE 70 is the lowest in the group and doesn't fit that framework.

recommendations.summary: Chlup, Gaborik, Nash, Klesla and Chistov are getting the games they've earned. No action needed.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 16.1 MPG and 38 pts at 19 on the second line, Gaborik 20 MPG and 81 pts on the first, Nash 12.5 MPG and 33 pts on the third. These are correct.

recommendations.summary: McCabe at 0.47 pts/g over 64 games on 4 years and $3M is the loudest defensive sell heading into the offseason.
recommendations.rationale: 1.42 to 0.47 is not an age decline at 29. No recovery since January. Four years of cap at $3M for a player below top-pair rates.

recommendations.summary: Salo at 0.17 pts/g over 27 games at 30 with $2.6M x 2 is below fourth-pair production and should be moved.
recommendations.rationale: 0.40 to 0.17 with minutes falling from 20.3 to 14.6. Two years of money on a collapsed 30-year-old D.

recommendations.summary: Klesla at 0.30 pts/g over 64 games at 22 is declining on a second consecutive season; trade him before his contract forces a decision.
recommendations.rationale: 0.50 to 0.30 with minutes flat at 14.7. At 22 the expected direction is up, not down.

recommendations.summary: Either commit 12+ MPG to Spacek or stop dressing him; 6.2 MPG at 0.33 pts/g develops nobody and has now cost him his early-season rate.
recommendations.rationale: 0.55 to 0.33 while minutes fell from 16.0 to 6.2. Raised four times since February 12th with no movement.

recommendations.summary: Either return Spezza to 10+ MPG in games we can afford or accept the full season is lost; 5.3 MPG has not moved in five raises.
recommendations.rationale: 0.43 to 0.38 on 5.3 MPG, down from 9.1. At 21 with elite potential, this is a wasted development year.

recommendations.summary: Stahle finally got 4 games and 17.8 MPG; keep dressing him through March so the GM can grade him before the offseason.
recommendations.rationale: Was zero games at January 25th. Four games at 20 with 96 potential is the start of what should be 15+ before the season ends.

recommendations.summary: Plan next season with Sundin at under 18 MPG; his minutes rose from 16.9 to 21.2 while his rate dropped from 1.46 to 0.95 at 34.
recommendations.rationale: The third-line endurance ceiling forces the top nine to carry more, but 21 MPG at 34 with declining production is unsustainable. Next year's line construction must solve this.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny at 0.83 pts/g on 19.9 MPG at 36 is at the end of his run as a daily top-six driver; plan the top six without him next year.
recommendations.rationale: 1.62 to 0.83, the steepest veteran decline. Same pattern at 38 for Roberts (1.29 to 0.85). Both need reduced roles or replacement next season.

recommendations.summary: No change for Chlup; he is earning the top-nine spot at 0.75 pts/g on 17.8 MPG at 19.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62 to 0.75 while minutes went from 11.0 to 17.8. He is doing the thing young players are not supposed to do: improving under increased load.

recommendations.summary: Room is healthy at 96-100 for all dressed players; no morale-driven lineup changes needed for Carolina.
recommendations.rationale: Winning streak lifted the group. Only Spezza at 86 is below 96 and that is a deliberate GM decision from Jan 15. Spacek at 92 is the one to watch if wins dry up, but no action tonight.

recommendations.summary: Accept the 51 faceoff mean on L4; at 6.6 MPG it is a short-shift unit and rebuilding two lines to fix it costs more than the draws lose.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 74 faceoffs is the only upgrade available and moving him down costs L3 both a faceoff win and its stamina anchor at 85. Short shifts mitigate the draw problem.

recommendations.summary: All eight units are built from players who suit them. The scoring lines score, the checking units check, the PP has shooters and a quarterback.
recommendations.rationale: P1 has Gaborik 99 playmaking and Kaberle quarterbacking. K1 has two 83-checkers plus Sundin's 90 faceoffs. L1/L2 are scoring lines with 90+ offensive grade up front. No misfit to correct.

recommendations.summary: The roster's best toughness is 72 (McCabe). No player above that. This team has no physical element for a playoff series.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe 72, Roberts 71, Abid 71, Fischer 70. Against a heavy team in April, there is nobody to deliver a hit and change the game's temperature. No lineup arrangement fixes this.

recommendations.summary: Sundin at 90 is the only 85+ faceoff man on the roster. Next best is Chlup at 79. Injury to Sundin leaves no one to win draws.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 90, Chlup 79, Roberts 75, Richards 74. A one-man faceoff operation is fragile. A second 85+ centre is the depth gap.

recommendations.summary: Carolina is a bad team on a seven-game losing streak giving up 3.40 a night. Our lines are outgrading them on every unit; no adjustment improves the win probability.
recommendations.rationale: Their top line (O'Neill 85, Brind'Amour 81, Sykora 80) faces Sundin/Gaborik/Roberts (89/96/86). Auto-pairing puts Fischer (CHKG 90, SPEE 93) on D1 against Ozolinsh (SPEE 91), which covers their only skating threat. The D-pair slot order is already correct.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour. No fatigue icon, 92 OVR, opponent scores 2.10 per game.
recommendations.rationale: Checked the streak cell — Belfour carries no goalie-tired marker. Against a team that generates 2.10 per game and is on a seven-game losing streak, this is a routine start.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays the loudest sell but wait for deadline or summer; his season total of 0.83 still has market value while the recent window of ~0.36 erodes it daily.
recommendations.rationale: 53 points in 64 games (0.83) but the Jan 26 rate of 0.96 has bled down through 14 recent games at ~0.36 pace. At 29 with $3M x 4, the selling window narrows each week. Eminger unchanged at 0.43 on an expiring $1.2M (sell now before UFCA). Salo at 0.30 and not dressed is a straight cut.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly in the bottom six to resolve the toughness gap at zero cost.
recommendations.rationale: The displayed 0-at-80+ toughness is a form artifact; stored grades put six players above 80. Tucker at stored TOUG 84 / CHKG 88 is currently in no unit and costs nothing.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Jackman from STL via the Belfour trade to give the defence a third D above 84 checking.
recommendations.rationale: The coach's structural gap is no third D above 84 CHKG. Roberts (86) and McCabe (86) are the only two. Jackman provides a third top-pair checker and was accepted by the GM on Feb 21 as both a Belfour return and a rival-weakening move.

recommendations.summary: Once a third top-pair D arrives, move Svehla (36, 92 CHKG base, $3.60M, expiring) for a pick via the over-80 mechanic before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is redundant if a Jackman-type D arrives. He is the club's second cleanest over-80 expiring pick-recovery asset after Belfour and his value walks in July.

recommendations.summary: Do not spend deadline currency on faceoffs. Richards at 70 FACE is the internal answer and the gap is tolerable for a playoff run.
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin (90) is above 80 in faceoffs but no available 85+ centre is realistic to acquire at this point. The GM's Feb 23 acceptance of Richards at third-line centre is sufficient.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Doan, Fleury or Bell for toughness. The gap is a form reading, not a structural deficiency.
recommendations.rationale: Six players carry stored TOUG above 80. The Feb 21 finding with high confidence confirmed this. Dressing Tucker solves the only actual availability problem.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour before March 19 for a draft pick or young player; he is 92 base, expiring, and the club's largest pick-recovery asset.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at $6.50M expiring qualifies for the over-80 expiring mechanic. Without moving him, Toronto gets zero draft picks from his departure in July. The GM already confirmed he is a chip worried about retirement.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla before March 19; he is 36, $3.60M, expiring, 92 CHKG, and a clean over-80 pick-recovery asset.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla at 36 with $3.60M expiring is the second-largest pick-recovery asset after Belfour. His value walks in July. A contender needing a shutdown D at the deadline pays a pick.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik on 5-6 years in July at whatever it costs; at 80 points and $1.10M he is the roster's cheapest star.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik is 23, 80 points in 63 games, POTE 90, expiring. Without a 5-6 year lock he enters July open and every club with payroll will chase him. This is the single highest-leverage re-signing on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards on 5-6 years in July; at 24 with 55 points and $1.00M expiring he is the centre after Sundin.
recommendations.rationale: Richards is 24, POTE 88, 55 points in 61 GP on $1.00M expiring. He is the next man up at centre when Sundin declines. Letting him test the market is a luxury the club cannot afford.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash on 5-6 years in July; 20 years old, 32 points, POTE 95, expiring at $1.20M.
recommendations.rationale: Nash is the youngest top-nine forward on the roster. His price will be low in July because he is 20 with one year of 32 points. By next July he may be a 40-point player and the price doubles.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger on 5-6 years in July; 21, POTE 99, 20 points in 45 GP, expiring at $1.20M.
recommendations.rationale: Eminger is the highest-potential defenceman the club has ever had. GM vetoed trading him in January specifically because his ceiling is unknown. The contract must match that belief.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 12+ MPG for the remaining 19 games; POTE 99 at 21 with 5.3 MPG is a wasted season that compounds when he enters the re-signing window unproven.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza's morale sits at 86 and his production (0.38 pts/g in limited chances) cannot be evaluated for the July contract negotiation. Playing him now gives the GM information before he offers a 4-5 year deal.

recommendations.summary: Open the Belfour-for-Hejduk negotiation with Colorado before March 19. Hejduk at 91 base, 33, $2.50M with two years is the best identified return: a top-line RW on two years of control at a reasonable salary.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, 39 years old. The retirement risk means his value walks in July if he does not play again. Colorado at 27-23 needs a backup goalie and the GM's own Feb 21 conversation produced Hejduk as their offer. Hejduk passes the GM's stated test: good, locked, reasonable salary, multiple years.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts at the deadline for a draft pick using the over-80 expiring mechanic. At 38 with 87 base, we will not re-sign him and a fourth-rounder or better strengthens a roster with no picks better than a fourth.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts reads 87 base and 87 overall, expiring, $2.70M, age 38. The manual's over-80 mechanic converts him into a pick. Keeping him through the playoffs is defensible but his playoff minutes should be limited at 38 and the pick capital serves the dynasty longer.

recommendations.summary: Hold Svehla through the playoffs. His 92 CHKG is the only thing between Toronto and the coach's third-pair checking gap, and the pick he would fetch at 36 is worth less than a playoff run with a sound third pair.
recommendations.rationale: The coach reports no third defenceman above 84 CHKG. Svehla at 92 CHKG is that player. Moving him at the deadline fills a dynasty pick need but exposes the playoff defenceman rotation. He will walk in July regardless, so the pick opportunity costs a deep run.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to five or six years at season end. He is 23 with 91 base and POTE 90 on $1.10M — the single most important contract on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik at 91 base and $1.10M with one year left is the cheapest star-caliber asset in the league. Allowing him to hit free agency at 24 invites a bidding war that will cost three times the current salary.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards (24), Kaberle (26), Eminger (21, POTE 99) and Nash (20) on five to six years at season end. All four are young core pieces whose current salaries ($1.00-1.90M) must be locked before they price up.
recommendations.rationale: The summer of 2005 has 15 contracts expiring worth roughly $25M. Staggering the stars and top prospects on five to six years while depth goes on two to three prevents the next renewal cluster.

recommendations.proposed: Chistov, Upshall, Alexeev, Abid, Smirnov, Colaiacovo
recommendations.summary: Re-sign the depth group (Chistov, Upshall, Alexeev, Abid, Smirnov) on two to three years and Colaiacovo on three to five at season end, staggered from the stars' deals.
recommendations.rationale: Six depth players on short deals keeps their expiries from landing in the same summer as Gaborik, Richards, Kaberle, Eminger and Nash. Total cost stays under $5M for the group.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour two years at $3.0-3.5M at season end. He will likely decline; accept the walk and move on with Luongo and Tellqvist.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's February 15 order was to offer reduced salary at renewal and accept he probably will not take it. If he walks, Luongo (91 base, 25, two years) and Tellqvist (POTE high 90s, $0.80M) cover both positions.

recommendations.summary: The Luongo and DiPietro monitoring task (asked January 19, due February 20) is complete. Luongo is on the roster at 91 base with two years left. DiPietro at 79 base with a 3.65 GAA is not a realistic target and NYI will re-sign. The January 15 goalie mandate is fulfilled.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo arrived by February 7. DiPietro's production this season (7-12-0, 3.65 GAA, 79 base) shows potential not translating and NYI at 64 points will hold him. No further monitoring needed.

recommendations.summary: Execute the Belfour-for-Jackman trade already agreed on Feb 21: Jackman (STL, 24, 80 base, CHKG 90, TOUG 89, $700K, 3 years) for Belfour.
recommendations.rationale: GM accepted Jackman on Feb 21 as the Belfour return. Jackman meets the criteria of 'good but locked on reasonable salary for a couple of years' — 3 years at $700K. His CHKG 90 solves the coach's third-pair checking gap immediately.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 92 pts/57 GP, $1.10M expiring) as the primary scoring target; ATL cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 62 pts with 11 expiring deals must liquidate. Heatley is the highest-scoring expiring player on the board at 1.61 ppg. Package logic: Svehla plus Chistov gives ATL a rebuild D and cheap centre, funded by the $3.60M salary relief Svehla provides ATL's payroll.

recommendations.summary: If ATL retains Heatley, pivot to Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 21, 89 base, 100 pts/60 GP, $1.10M expiring) — the better long-term asset of the ATL pair.
recommendations.rationale: 100 points at 21 with $1.10M expiring is the best trajectory value on the board. ATL's binary means one of the two is available. Kovalchuk at 21 has 5-6 prime years ahead; Heatley at 24 is closer to peak.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Havlat (OTT, LW, 23, 87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, $900K expiring) as the cheapest 80-point option; the Chara veto does not extend to him.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 60 pts with 11 expiring deals and $28.38M profit are comfortable sellers. 80 points at $900K is the best production-to-cost ratio outside ATL. Package: Tucker (29, $1.30M, CHKG 88, TOUG 84, currently in no unit) plus the fourth-rounder gives OTT physical depth and a pick.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Samsonov (BOS, LW, 26, 89 base, 92 pts/54 GP, $1.90M expiring) — available only if BOS decides to sell at 70 points.
recommendations.rationale: 92 points in 54 games at $1.90M is elite production at a moderate cost. BOS at 70 pts with 13 expiring deals and $26.56M profit could go either way. Acceptance is genuinely uncertain; do not build a plan on him.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Komisarek (MTL, D, 23, 77 base, 70 pts/64 GP, POTE 91, $1.10M expiring) — a 23-year-old offensive D from a 50-point club with 15 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: 70 points in 64 games as a 23-year-old defenceman with POTE 91 is a top-pair asset that will be 85+ base within two seasons. MTL at 50 pts cannot re-sign him. The Feb 13 package (St. Jacques plus Safronov plus the fourth-rounder) may still be viable if those players remain on roster.

recommendations.summary: Sign-and-flip rental: Conroy (CGY, C, 33, 85 base, 77 pts/64 GP, FACE 94, $2.00M expiring) for a playoff run only. Fallback if ATL and OTT targets fall through.
recommendations.rationale: FACE 94 is the best faceoff number available anywhere. 77 points in 64 games at 33 is a pure rental — he goes nowhere in July. Package: Chistov plus the fourth-rounder. Only worth it if we cannot land a younger scoring target.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla (36, 83 base, $3.60M expiring) to a contender for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic. His CHKG 83 is below the coach's 84 threshold, so Jackman's arrival makes him surplus.
recommendations.rationale: The over-80 mechanic allows trading an expiring player for a pick without knowing what the other side needs. A 75+ point club needing a third-pair D for a playoff run is the natural buyer. This generates the pick capital Toronto lacks — only one fourth-rounder currently held.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Thornton (BOS, 94 base) — his 94 base and 73 pts/47 GP make him the most complete player available, but BOS at 70 points with 13 expiring deals is likely a playoff team, and any package would conflict with the Belfour trade.
recommendations.rationale: Thornton closes scoring, TOUG 89, and CHKG 90 simultaneously, but the acceptance probability is low and the cost is a non-starter (Belfour plus another piece at $4.00M salary absorption). The Jackman trade already closes checking; the ATL targets close scoring. Thornton adds nothing that cannot be had more cheaply.

recommendations.current: Tucker (29, LW, $1.30M, 2yr, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, 1 GP) + 4th round pick
recommendations.proposed: Martin Havlat (OTT, LW, 23, 87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, $900K expiring)
recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker plus the 4th-rounder to Ottawa for Havlat; OTT at 60 pts with 11 expiring deals cannot re-sign him and gets a physical winger with two years of control.
recommendations.rationale: Havlat's 80 points in 63 games at $900K is the best scoring-per-dollar on the deadline board. OTT is a full seller (60 pts, 11 expiring). Tucker gives them CHKG 92 and TOUG 88 with 2 years at $1.30M, useful for their rebuild. Toronto net down $400K salary and gain a top-six winger for the playoff run. Acceptance uncertain because Havlat is a high-profile expiring asset and OTT may want more than a 4th-round pick.

recommendations.current: Svehla (36, D, 83 base, 92 CHKG stored, $3.60M expiring)
recommendations.proposed: Draft pick (round uncertain, likely 3rd or 4th) from Colorado
recommendations.summary: Move Svehla to Colorado for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic; COL are a contender with D needs and an established willingness to trade from strength.
recommendations.rationale: The GM confirmed on Feb 21 that Colorado's GM offered Hejduk for Belfour, proving he pays for playoff help. Svehla's 92 stored CHKG fills their top-4 D need for the playoffs. The guide notes above-80 expiring players can be moved for picks. Toronto frees $3.60M and recovers capital that otherwise walks July 1. If this lands before the Havlat deal, the incoming pick replaces our 4th as currency, preserving net pick count.

recommendations.current: St. Jacques (24, D, $0.80M, 2yr, POTE 94, 1 GP) + Safronov (24, D, $0.90M, 3yr, POTE 91, 3 GP) + 4th round pick (or incoming pick from Svehla deal)
recommendations.proposed: Karel Komisarek (MTL, D, 23, 77 base, 70 pts/64 GP, POTE 91, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Offer St. Jacques, Safronov and a pick to Montreal for Komisarek; MTL at 46 points with 15 expiring deals cannot retain him and accepts unproven youth for their rebuild.
recommendations.rationale: Komisarek's 70 points at D at age 23 with POTE 91 makes him a top-pair offensive D in development. MTL's 15 expiring contracts signal full liquidation; they will not re-sign him. St. Jacques and Safronov give them two 24-year-old D prospects (POTE 94 and 91) plus a pick for their lottery year. Toronto gains a long-term D partner for Eminger at $1.10M for one year with a re-sign option. Acceptance uncertain because 4 combined NHL games on the return pieces may read as low value.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task is closed: Luongo arrived at 94 overall with 42 starts, DiPietro's play confirms he is not a target.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 94 overall, age 25, $1.60M, 2 years fulfills the Jan 15 mandate. DiPietro at 79 base, 0.849 SP, 21 GP shows no development toward NHL quality. GM's Feb 19 order closes the topic.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs 12+ minutes in at least a few of the remaining 19 games; morale at 86 is the first sign the minutes shortfall is hurting.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21, 7.5 MPG across 37 games, currently scratched. Morale 86 is the lowest of any young player. The minutes are below the 10 MPG band for his calibre.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle for at least one game in the remaining 19; POTE 96 at 20 with 4 career games is the biggest untapped asset on the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: 4 GP all season averaging 17.8 MPG in those 4. POTE 96, age 20. Flagged since January 25 with no movement. One or two games before the deadline costs nothing and starts the evaluation.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov at 0 GP with POTE 70 is not a development loss; sitting is the right call at his level.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest POTE among the young group. No production to justify games. The GM's rotation philosophy is working correctly here.

recommendations.summary: Give Spacek 12+ MPG for the final two weeks or accept the season as a development loss.
recommendations.rationale: His rate collapsed from 0.55 to 0.34 pts/g while minutes fell from 16.0 to 6.4. Unlike Spezza, his production is also falling, not just his ice. At 19, 6 MPG for three months wastes the year.

recommendations.summary: Flag Richards' decline for off-season planning: 1.08 to 0.78 pts/g at 24 on flat minutes.
recommendations.rationale: At 24 the expected direction is up. A 28 percent rate decline with no role change is a genuine trend, not noise, and it affects how his contract is valued next summer.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Nash's rate through February; 0.83 to 0.46 on flat minutes at 20 is a second-year wall or early-season inflation.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes are unchanged (12.9 to 12.5) but his rate halved. If he finishes the season near 0.46, the 24-game early window was not predictive and next season's expectations need adjusting.

recommendations.summary: Keep Stahle dressed for the remaining games; 4 games at 17.8 MPG is the first data point on a POTE 96 defenceman.
recommendations.rationale: He went from zero games to four at 17.8 MPG. No production yet (0.00 pts/g) but at 20 with that potential, every game from here is tracking information for next season.

recommendations.summary: No change; Chlup's 0.62 to 0.77 pts/g on doubled minutes confirms the top-nine move.
recommendations.rationale: Trend held since the Feb 23 note. He is producing 0.77 at 17.5 MPG at 19. Nothing to adjust.

recommendations.proposed: Spezza at 10+ MPG in the lineup
recommendations.summary: Spezza at 86 morale and 7.5 MPG is the only morale issue on the roster; put him in at 10+ or accept the number stays down.
recommendations.rationale: Even at 70-79 calibre the expected band is 10 MPG; he gets 7.5 as a scratch. Morale at 86 costs him one point off his overall every game. Raised repeatedly; GM has not acted. This is the only lever that moves his morale.

recommendations.summary: All eight units are built correctly for their jobs. No composition change needed for Detroit.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has skill plus checking plus faceoffs. L2 is the offensive line by design. L3 has Nash at 84 checking as the shutdown anchor. K1 fields three 84-checkers. Nothing here is misassembled.

recommendations.summary: We need a second centre who wins faceoffs at 85+; the roster has nobody above 80 besides Sundin.
recommendations.rationale: Only 4 skaters on the roster exceed 75 in faceoffs (Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Roberts 76, Richards 75). L2 draws at 58 mean against every opponent's second centre. This is unfixable by line arrangement — we are short a drawman.

recommendations.summary: Either commit 12+ MPG to Spacek or stop dressing him; 6.6 MPG develops nobody and has now gone unaddressed for six recommendations.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek is at 0.36 pts/g on 6.6 MPG. He is dressed but not playing enough to grow or to contribute. The middle ground is the worst outcome for his morale expectation and his development.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour (93 OVR) over Ouellet (82) against Hasek (91). Check fatigue icon before game per routine.
recommendations.rationale: Goalie gap is +2 with Belfour, -9 with Ouellet against a 91 OVR Hasek who keeps bad teams in games. Belfour's morale is 99 and OVR is 93, he should be fine, but check the icon per standard procedure.

recommendations.summary: No line changes. Our top two lines outclass theirs, our depth matches three-for-three, and Detroit's PP is 16.6%.
recommendations.rationale: Detroit is 27-23-5 with 2.60 GA per game, their L4 is three guys at 67-71 OVR, and we won the one meeting 9-1. Fischer/McCabe on D1 handles Lidstrom/Hatcher; no D pair reorder is warranted.

recommendations.summary: Keep Spacek in. Their fourth line (Pesonen 67, Williams 67, Mowers 71) is the weakest assignment in the league this week.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek at 76 OVR against three 67-71 opponents is a favorable development matchup. The game classification here is 'game we can afford to develop in' given Detroit's bottom-six quality.

recommendations.summary: McCabe remains the loudest sell: 0.84 pts/g at 29 with $3M x 4 remaining and a steady decline from 0.96 in late January.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate has dropped 0.12 since January 26 (0.96 → 0.84) across 13 more games, gaining only 5 points in that stretch (0.38 recent). Four years of $3M for a declining 29-year-old is the roster's biggest cap liability.

recommendations.summary: Eminger is back on the sell list. His recovery did not hold: 1 point in his last 6 games, season rate now 0.44.
recommendations.rationale: Was off the list on Feb 19 at 0.57 recent. Now 20 points in 45 games (0.44 season, 0.17 recent over last 6). At 21 with an expiring $1.2M deal the sell window is now before he becomes a cheap UFCA.

recommendations.summary: Klesla stays on the list: 0.37 pts/g at age 22 with minutes flat at 14.8 and a second declining season.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate 23/63 = 0.37, barely moved from 0.38 last week. At 22 the expected direction is up. Two years at $0.9M makes him movable for future value before the contract forces the decision.

recommendations.summary: Stahle has broken into the lineup with 4 games played since having zero before; keep giving him ice.
recommendations.rationale: He had 0 GP as of late January and now has 4. Slow progress for a POTE-96 20-year-old but movement in the right direction. No sell case here.

recommendations.slot: fourth-line defence pair or seventh defenceman
recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker in a defensive unit every night; his 83 CHKG is the fourth-best on the roster and he currently sits in no line.
recommendations.rationale: With Svehla likely moving by March 19 (expiring, $3.60M, 36), checking depth drops from 6 to 5 at 80+. Tucker closes the gap at zero trade cost. The coach's own report notes he is in no unit.

recommendations.summary: Toughness is a confirmed structural gap (best base TOUG 73, zero at 80+) with no internal fix and all external targets either vetoed by GM or production-poor.
recommendations.rationale: Chara is vetoed (Feb 19), Avery's 0.11 ppg kills his case, Bell was killed on position grounds. The gap is real but the market options the GM has already rejected were the best available. Recommend acknowledging the gap and hoping Eminger's development (POTE 99, 21) closes it over two seasons rather than forcing a deadline deal that fails on other criteria.

recommendations.summary: Faceoff depth is one man deep (Sundin 90, next best Chlup 75); flag as the priority need for summer centre acquisition.
recommendations.rationale: Playoff matchups against elite centres will win zones off the draw. No one on the current roster or on the GM-approved target list closes this. Any summer centre must carry 80+ FACE.

recommendations.summary: Spezza appears in no role group at any grade above 70; at POTE 99 and 7.5 MPG this is a lost development year the coach has flagged six consecutive times.
recommendations.rationale: The coach's position is clear. This is not a coverage gap today but it is the most obvious case of unused potential on the roster. Either ice him 10+ MPG or accept the year is burned; the coach says burned.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to 5-6 years the moment his contract opens in July; at 80 points and $1.10M he is the single most valuable asset on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 15 players expire the same July. Gaborik is the highest-production player among them (80 pts/62 GP, POTE 90, age 23). If he plays next season and walks, the loss is unrecoverable.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash to 5-6 years this July; at 20 with POTE 95 and 32 points on $1.20M, his renewal cost doubles the moment he plays every night.
recommendations.rationale: Same July cluster. Nash is younger than Gaborik and his POTE 95 means his next contract will be dramatically more expensive if he develops on schedule. Lock now at rookie-window pricing.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to 5-6 years this July; 55 points in 60 games at $1.00M and age 24 makes him the cheapest top-pairing centre in the league.
recommendations.rationale: His POTE is 88 which caps his ceiling below Chlup and Spezza, but his production today (55 pts, 70 FACE) makes him the best centre available on this roster for the next 3-4 years. Lock the value.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger and Upshall to 5-6 years this July at their current $1.20M rate before their next season moves their price.
recommendations.rationale: Both 21, both POTE 99, both $1.20M with one year left. They are not yet stars but their potential means next-year pricing will be $3-4M. Lock now and accept them as trade bait later if they do not develop.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour ($6.50M, 92 base, expiring) and Svehla ($3.60M, 92 CHKG, expiring) before March 19 to recover two draft picks and free $10.10M.
recommendations.rationale: Both are over-80 expiring assets whose value evaporates in July. Toronto owns no pick better than a fourth-rounder; these two trades are the only pick-recovery vehicles available this season.

recommendations.summary: Do not extend or trade Sundin (34, 5yrs) or Mogilny (36, 2yrs); let their contracts run and resolve naturally.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin carries to 39, Mogilny to 38. No extension needed, no trade value to recover (both expiring beyond this season). They produce 140 combined points now and the succession plan (Chlup, Spezza, Spacek at centre; Alexeev, Nash at wing) is already aging into those roles.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour before March 19 for a multi-year player; Colorado has offered Hejduk, STL for Jackman on rival-weakness logic.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 92 base, $6.50M, 1yr, 39. If he retires or walks in July we get nothing. GM is actively exploring; this is the deadline's central negotiation.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla before March 19 via the over-80 expiring mechanic to recover a draft pick.
recommendations.rationale: 36 years old, $3.60M, 1yr, 92 CHKG. Over-80 expiring players can be traded for picks. Toronto owns no pick better than a 5th-rounder.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts before March 19 via the over-80 expiring mechanic to recover a second draft pick.
recommendations.rationale: 38 years old, $2.70M, 1yr. Won't be re-signed. Over-80 expiring means pick-recovery eligible.

recommendations.summary: Renew Gaborik on 5-6 years at season end. Highest-priority summer deal.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base at 23 on $1.10M expiring. A 5-6 year lock keeps a 23-year-old scorer cheap through his prime.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: 24, $1.00M expiring, already the faceoff center the coach relies on beyond Sundin.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: 26, $1.90M, top-pairing D entering prime. Must be locked before other clubs find him in July.

recommendations.summary: Renew Eminger on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: 21, $1.20M, POTE 99, GM-protected. This is the franchise D of the next five years.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: 20, $1.20M, young core forward. Lock long while the price is still one million.

recommendations.summary: Renew Colaiacovo on 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: 22, POTE 96 but coach reducing ice. Cheap short deal buys development time without a long commitment.

recommendations.summary: Renew depth five on 2-3 year deals.
recommendations.rationale: All under 25, all under $1.20M. Short deals keep payroll flexible and let development sort itself.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist on 2-3 years as backup goalie.
recommendations.rationale: 25, $0.80M, POTE 99, GM standing order to develop him. Cheap insurance behind Luongo.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue the December 22 package; it is dead because Toronto no longer owns the 2nd, 3rd or 4th round picks it required.
recommendations.rationale: Pick table shows TOR R2 to DET, R3 to WSH, R4 to PIT. The Mogilny+R2/Sillinger/R3/Sutton+R4 structure cannot be executed.

recommendations.summary: Open negotiations late February for a scoring forward from a seller to address team-wide depth scoring.
recommendations.rationale: GM's Feb 19 order identifies depth scoring as the core problem. Toronto are 1st in the East with 17 points of cushion — buying is low-risk.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Fleury (CHI, RW, 89 base, 95 TOUG, $4.30M expiring, 42 pts/55 GP) from a 51-point club with 10 expiring deals who cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only 95 TOUG player on a seller in the league and the only player who closes the toughness gap AND adds 0.76 ppg scoring in one move. CHI's alternative is losing him in July for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Conroy (CGY, C, 85 base, 94 FACE, 80 CHKG, $2.00M expiring, 73 pts/62 GP) from the league's worst club desperate to shed salary.
recommendations.rationale: 94 FACE with 73 points is the best two-way centre on any seller. CGY at 48 points with 10 expiring deals have no reason to keep him. Rental-only but ideal for a playoff run.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Doan (PHX, RW, 87 base, 88 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $2.40M expiring, 45 pts/60 GP) from a 60-point club with 14 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: 88 TOUG and 93 CHKG simultaneously close two gaps no other available player does. PHX at $11M profit with 14 expiring deals cannot re-sign him and must deal him before March 19.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell (CHI, LW, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $900K, 2 years) as the cheapest re-signable toughness body available.
recommendations.rationale: At $900K with two years of control he provides a fourth-line checking presence tonight and retains trade value at 27. CHI are selling and he is expendable.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Jackman (STL, D, 80 base, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, $700K, 3 years) as the Belfour trade return the GM identified on Feb 21.
recommendations.rationale: 25 years old, 3 years of control at $700K, closes toughness on defence. STL at 63 points and profitable may engage if they are out of the race by March. The GM already endorsed him over Hejduk.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bates (NYI, C, 83 base, 94 FACE, 83 CHKG, $900K expiring, 32 pts/46 GP) as the budget faceoff rental if Conroy's price is too high.
recommendations.rationale: Same draw rate as Conroy at less than half the salary. NYI at 60 points with 13 expiring deals will deal him. 0.70 ppg is adequate third-line production for a playoff push.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Marchant (CBJ, C, 88 base, 94 FACE, $4.88M expiring, 68 pts/60 GP) only if Conroy and Bates are blocked on price.
recommendations.rationale: Highest-scoring faceoff specialist on any seller (68 pts) but $4.88M requires sending back real salary from Toronto. CBJ at 59 points with 9 expiring deals will deal him but need a salary match.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Souray (MTL, D, 79 base, 89 TOUG, 91 CHKG, $1.40M expiring, 20 pts/50 GP) as the cheapest defensive toughness available.
recommendations.rationale: Montreal at 50 points with 15 expiring deals (most in league) will deal anyone. 91 CHKG is playoff-useful against a power forward line, and at $1.40M the salary return needed is small.

recommendations.proposed: Jackman (STL, D, 25, 80 base, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, $700K, 3 years)
recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour to STL for Jackman: closes toughness gap by 16 points, recovers a pick, frees $5.80M, and gets a 25-year-old with three years of control on a $700K deal.
recommendations.rationale: STL at 63 points need playoff goalie insurance; Belfour is 18-3, 2.27 GAA, .916 SP. STL profitable at $11.68M can absorb $6.50M for a rental. Jackman is good but replaceable on a 63-point roster. GM stated this as his preferred return on Feb 21.

recommendations.proposed: Conroy (CGY, C, 31, 94 FACE, 85 base, 80 CHKG, $2.00M expiring, 73 pts/62 GP)
recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov plus the 4th to CGY for Conroy: 94 FACE closes the 15-point faceoff cliff and 73-point production upgrades the second line for $0.90M net.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 48 points (worst in league) with 10 expiring deals will not re-sign Conroy at 31. They get a 21-year-old with POTE 95 and 89/88 speed grades, which is rebuilding gold. We gain the only available player above 90 FACE outside Sundin.

recommendations.current: Tucker (LW, 29, $1.30M, 83 CHKG, in no unit) + Colaiacovo (D, 22, POTE 99, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.proposed: Doan (PHX, RW, 87 base, 88 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $2.40M expiring, 45 pts/60 GP)
recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker plus Colaiacovo to PHX for Doan: salary-neutral swap that closes toughness AND checking simultaneously, from a 60-point team with 14 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: Doan's 88 TOUG and 93 CHKG are the only player who closes both gaps in one move. Phoenix cannot re-sign him. Tucker contributes nothing in the current lineup; Colaiacovo is POTE 99 but the D pipeline is deep (5 players at 94+). Salary is exactly neutral at $2.40M each side.

recommendations.summary: Close the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task; Luongo is at 94 and 42 GP healthy, DiPietro has not developed into a viable target.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo added 5 games since Feb 7 with no injury and no grade movement. DiPietro remains below 86 overall at NYI (24-28) with 79 base and 3.65 GAA. The Feb 19 order closed this file; nothing has changed to reopen it.
