recommendations.summary: Move Spezza up to third-line centre to bring him above 12 MPG; his morale at 86 is the room's lowest among dressed players and his minutes at 7.8 are below any development threshold.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza is 21 with 14 points in 34 games on 7.8 MPG. A player his age and production needs 12+ to consolidate growth. The -4 morale drop this window confirms the sheet: he knows he's underused.

recommendations.summary: No change for the rest of the room. The dips from Sundin, Richards and Alexeev all recovered in this save, meaning they were results-driven and the winning streak is self-correcting them.
recommendations.rationale: 24 of 32 players are at 96 or above with upward or stable morale. The room is where it should be.

recommendations.summary: Aebischer at 81 is below any line-change fix. Either he plays somewhere or his grades stay depressed by 2 when called in relief.
recommendations.rationale: 81 morale costs 2 points across every grade. At 19 GP this season he is not a third-stringer; he is a backup without a job. This is a roster decision, not a lineup one.

recommendations.summary: Safronov at 95 and dropping 5 points, with 3 games played all season, is a decision the GM needs to make: dress him or deal him. The current state burns him.
recommendations.rationale: 23 years old, 0 points in 3 games, scratched indefinitely. Morale is sliding and his window is closing. This was flagged in December and has gotten worse.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker and put him on K1 in place of Mogilny.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker carries 81 checking, the fourth-best on the roster and the third-best forward. Mogilny is a 92 scoring winger on a PK unit where his role is to block shots he does not want to block. The chemistry cost is minimal — PK units turn over faster than even-strength lines.

recommendations.summary: No change to L1, L2, P1, P2, K2, or the goalie.
recommendations.rationale: Those units are built correctly. L2's faceoff mean of 61 is a roster gap, not a composition error — Richards at 75 is the best draw man available on that unit.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour in net Monday at Washington.
recommendations.rationale: Their shot quality comes from Jagr (SHPW 95) and Gonchar (SHPW 93, HERO 95). Belfour at OVR 93 with BRKA 95 and REBC 94 handles heavy shots better than Tellqvist at 75.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for Washington.
recommendations.rationale: Their PP is 9.8% (12/122) so PK personnel is irrelevant. Their first-line faceoff (Lang FACE 66, Jagr FACE 51) means Sundin at 89 wins those draws and controls zone time. Their third and fourth lines (OVR 68-79) are weaker than our third and fourth (OVR 71-83). The standard matchups already favor us.

recommendations.summary: Put Nash back in the lineup. 30 points in 34 games at 20 years old cannot sit.
recommendations.rationale: He's been scratched for 11 of 45 games despite producing at 0.88 pts/g. The healthy-scratch pattern from December 29 has recurred. No explanation justifies benching a kid scoring at that rate.

recommendations.summary: Move Spezza up to the third line and give him 12+ minutes a night.
recommendations.rationale: 7.8 MPG on the fourth line for a 99-potential player producing at 0.62 pts/g is the underuse pattern flagged January 5. He needs 12+ to consolidate what he's showing.

recommendations.summary: Safronov is 3 GP, 0 points, scratched at 23 years old. Name him in or release the spot.
recommendations.rationale: This has been raised since December 15 with no resolution. Three games and zero points means the current arrangement is to waste him. Either dress him and find a role, or tell him he's not in the plan.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov at 0 GP and 70 potential has no realistic path to games on this roster. Tell him plainly.
recommendations.rationale: He's behind Nash (30 pts), Chistov, and Koltsov at left wing with zero games played all season. Dressing him serves no purpose; releasing the spot helps someone else develop.

recommendations.summary: Spacek at 0.61 pts/g in 23 games at 19 is earning a regular spot but getting scratched. Decide if he's in the lineup.
recommendations.rationale: 14 points in 23 games with 91 potential at age 19. He plays well when dressed (13 MPG, half the games). Either make him a regular or explain what's holding him out.

recommendations.summary: Restore Spacek to 13+ MPG; I cut him to 10.2 while his rate climbed to 0.67 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: A 19-year-old producing 0.67 pts/g earns more ice, not less. I made a coaching error here and need to correct it.

recommendations.slot: winger on second or third line
recommendations.summary: Give Upshall 12+ MPG; his rate is 0.53 on 8.5 MPG, which exceeds the threshold he set himself in December.
recommendations.rationale: Memory from Jan 8 set 0.55 as the floor and he is at 0.53 over the full window, but his since-Dec rate is what matters and it is 0.53 with minutes cut, not earned. The Jan 8 note said he earned 12+.

recommendations.summary: Put Spezza in the lineup at 12+ MPG immediately; at 21 with 5.7 MPG we will never know what he is.
recommendations.rationale: Rate fell 0.43 to 0.38 while minutes fell 9.1 to 5.7 simultaneously. The Jan 5 memory set 12 MPG as the condition for his development; without it the window closes.

recommendations.summary: McCabe's collapse (1.42 to 0.67 pts/g) means we have no reliable first-pair partner for Eminger; the GM needs to look at the trade market or accept Colaiacovo there permanently.
recommendations.rationale: At 29, a drop of this size with no injury is not recoverable by February. The blue line's second spot is a gap the lineup cannot solve.

recommendations.summary: Sundin (0.90) and Mogilny (0.76) have both lost more than half their rate; plan the top six for the rest of the season and next season around a fading first line.
recommendations.rationale: The Dec 19 memory predicted a February scoring collapse and we are 5 weeks out. Richards, Gaborik and Chlup must shoulder the load now.

recommendations.summary: Safronov got 3 games and 0 points at 13.7 MPG; the GM needs to decide whether to keep running him or close the window.
recommendations.rationale: The Dec 15 memory said the window was closing. Three more games without production means we either commit to a longer look or move on.

recommendations.summary: Give Alexeev more shifts; promote him to L3 wing or give him the heaviest usage on L4. Target 12+ MPG.
recommendations.rationale: 25 points in 45 games at 9.1 MPG is second-line production in fourth-line minutes. Morale dropped 3 since Dec 28, consistent with the gap between his output and his ice.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza more of the fourth line's shifts, target 12+ MPG.
recommendations.rationale: 14 points in 34 games at 7.8 MPG with morale down 4 since Dec 28. He is under his 10 MPG band even if he is a 70-79 guy, and well under the 12+ threshold his development needs at 21.

recommendations.summary: GM needs to decide if Safronov is in or out. He's played 3 games all season and his morale is dropping.
recommendations.rationale: Down 5 to 95 with 3 GP at age 23. A 23-year-old with ability watching from the press box every game loses both morale and development time. No line change fixes this.

recommendations.summary: Sundin's -4 dip has recovered (+4 most recent). No change needed.
recommendations.rationale: At 17.9 MPG he is slightly under his likely 20 MPG band, but the upward bounce in the latest save shows the wins are fixing it. Revisit if he drops again.

recommendations.summary: We have three active skaters checking above 80 (McCabe 84, Fischer 84, Roberts 83) and they all play on L1 because we need them there. Tucker at 81 is the fourth option and he is scratched.
recommendations.rationale: No arrangement fixes this. L3 mean checking is 67. A true shutdown pair needs two 80+ players on the same blue line and we can only build one pair (McCabe/Fischer). The GM needs a trade target at checking centre or a physical second-pair D.

recommendations.summary: Sundin at 89 is the only player winning draws above 80. Chlup 78 is next, then Richards 75. We lose the dot on three of four lines every game.
recommendations.rationale: This has been the same since December 7th. No lineup fix exists. Fourth-line centres read 53 on the brief.

recommendations.summary: Put Tucker on the third line over Koltsov to raise L3 checking from 67 to something above 70 and free the roster's fourth-best checker for game action.
recommendations.rationale: Koltsov has failed the 0.60 pts/g recovery threshold (at 0.42 per my Jan 1 note). Tucker at 81 checking is the only player who changes L3's character. If Tucker is scratched for injury or morale reasons, disregard.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza and Upshall as much of the fourth line as their stamina allows. Their rates (0.62 and 0.69) justify 12+ MPG but the unit's stamina at 51 says be cautious about overloading both simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Both are producing above the development threshold and need minutes to consolidate. Rotate the load between them rather than pushing both at once. Upshall doubled his rate in five weeks; Spezza is climbing. Neither should be buried.

recommendations.summary: Play the same four lines. The matchups are already favorable as constructed.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts (CHKG 86, TOUG 88) already shadows Jagr (TOUG 62, CHKG 52) on L1. Sundin FACE 89 beats Lang FACE 66. Gaborik at OVR 97 is on L2 against their best remaining player Bondra at 86. Their blue line from position three down is OVR 66-75. No shuffle improves this.

recommendations.summary: Belfour starts Monday. Washington's PP at 12 on 122 means even a bad night in front is survivable.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at OVR 93 and ENDU 87 is rested after two days off. Their PP converts under 10%. Their scoring is Jagr, Bondra and Gonchar's shot — 3.6 per game — well within what our defensive structure can hold.

recommendations.summary: No player on the roster carries 80 base TOUG; acquire an 80+ power forward at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: The highest base toughness on the roster is 73 (Roberts, McCabe). Tucker's 92 is a form spike over a 70 base, confirmed. Chara at 88 TOUG and 89 CHKG is on a rebuilding Ottawa club with 11 expiring deals. Bertuzzi at 89 TOUG is available if Vancouver fall below .600.

recommendations.summary: Sundin at 90 FACE is the only faceoff man above 80; a second 80+ draw man is needed for the second and third centres.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup at 75, Roberts at 75, Richards at 70. Three lines will lose the draw against competent centres. Thornton at 82 FACE and 91 OVR is a seller target on a struggling Boston club.

recommendations.summary: Linen Tucker (83 CHKG) into a nightly role to bring the lined checking core to four at 82+.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker has 83 CHKG and 70 base TOUG at 29, and is on the roster but in no unit. Lining him gets the team from two lined checkers above 83 to three.

recommendations.summary: Two of the six 80+ checkers are 36 or older; the checking core will thin within two seasons.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 38 with 86 CHKG, Svehla is 36 with 83 CHKG. The only under-30 checkers at 80+ are McCabe (29), Tucker (29), Fischer (24) and Upshall (21). The 21-24 end barely clears the bar at 80 and 82.

recommendations.summary: Scoring, playmaking and speed are covered; no acquisition needed in those roles.
recommendations.rationale: 13 players at 80+ scoring, 12 at 80+ playmaking, 25 at 80+ speed. The trajectory concern is age (Mogilny 35, Sundin 33) not volume. Gaborik 92 and Afinogenov 90 carry the future.

recommendations.summary: Belfour and Aebischer are both above 0.895 SV; coverage is sufficient through the season.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour 2.42 GAA, .905 SV in 18 starts. Aebischer 2.62 GAA, .898 SV in 19. Tellqvist at 3.21 is a clear third. The question is the summer, not tonight.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup to a 5-6 year deal now, before his price rises.
recommendations.rationale: He is 18, POTE 95, 23 pts in 34 games on $2.34M with 2 years left; a full top-nine season erases the rookie-window price.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash and Kaberle on 5-6 year deals to break the 17-deal July cluster.
recommendations.rationale: All four expire in the same July ($1.10M, $1.00M, $1.20M, $1.90M) and carry the young core; long terms stop them renewing against each other.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour for a draft pick before March rather than releasing him in July.
recommendations.rationale: At 39, $6.50M expiring, CONS 50 he fits the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic; Aebischer (26, $0.50M) and Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) can cover the crease.

recommendations.summary: Move expiring veterans Roberts and Svehla for picks while they still hold trade value.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts (38, $2.70M) and Svehla (36, $3.60M) are both one-year deals 35-plus; trading them thins the 34+ line and the $18.30M it carries.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign one of Aebischer or Tellqvist on 2-3 years as the crease plan after Belfour leaves.
recommendations.rationale: Both are young and expiring; the guide warns good goalies are lost by forgetting them, so lock the keeper before July.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour before March: he is 39, $6.50M expiring, 91 overall, and the above-80-expiring mechanic guarantees pick value.
recommendations.rationale: He is the engine of the Chara package; if OTT decline, he still moves for a second-rounder alone. Aebischer is ready at 2.62 GAA in 19 starts.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Chara (80 base, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 27, $1.70M expiring) and Havlat (87 base, 61 pts in 42 GP, 23, $0.90M expiring) from OTT for Belfour plus the own first-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 15-19-4 with 11 expiring deals must sell. This solves toughness and adds top-six wing in one negotiation.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Kovalchuk (89 base, 78 pts in 41 GP, 21, $1.10M expiring) from ATL for the DET second-rounder plus Chistov.
recommendations.rationale: ATL cannot retain both Kovalchuk and Heatley on expiring deals. If they re-sign Heatley, Kovalchuk becomes available cheap.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Abid (LW, 25, $400K expiring, 86 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 54 pts in 43 GP) from PIT for a third-rounder plus Holden.
recommendations.rationale: He is the cheapest impact player on the seller board. PIT at 12-21-5 with 14 expiring deals must move him.

recommendations.summary: Move Safronov (23, 3 GP, 0 pts, morale down 5 to 95) at the deadline via the December fallback or elsewhere; he cannot develop sitting.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flagged him on January 8. He is the package-3 piece for Sutton if the January proposals die.

recommendations.current: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Kaberle, Upshall, Eminger, Colaiacovo
recommendations.summary: Lock seven young core players on 5-6 year deals in July 2005 at current rates to split the seventeen-contract cluster.
recommendations.rationale: These seven cost $8.70M combined at current rates; waiting one year when they are 20-22 and developing will double it.

recommendations.summary: Move Renberg (LW, 32, $2.00M expiring) at the deadline for a late pick or let him walk in July; do not re-sign at 32 on $2.00M.
recommendations.rationale: Two million for a 32-year-old winger who will not get younger. That money is better on a 22-year-old on a 5-year deal.

recommendations.summary: If Svehla (D, 36, $3.60M expiring) is not traded at the deadline, re-sign on 2 years at no more than $2.50M.
recommendations.rationale: 36 and $3.60M is the worst value on the expiring list. Two years caps the risk; if his play drops, he moves in July 2006.

recommendations.summary: Do not sell the deadline. At 73 points and 12 clear of second place, the only rational posture is to buy.
recommendations.rationale: The three proposals stack without overlapping assets. No reason to dismantle a 33-8-1 club.

recommendations.summary: Abid (PIT, LW, 24, 56 pts/44 GP, 87 TOUG, 87 CHKG, $400K expiring) remains the best value on the seller board; PIT at 12-21-5 with 14 expiring must move him.
recommendations.rationale: Solves toughness and adds a 1.27 pts/g top-nine scorer at $400K. PIT are the fifth-worst team with the most expiring deals in the Eastern Conference. Return: 3rd rounder plus Holden.

recommendations.summary: Savard (ATL, C, 27, 89 FACE, 48 pts/43 GP, $1.00M expiring) is a new sleeper who solves the faceoff gap and adds scoring at $1M on a full-rebuild ATL club.
recommendations.rationale: Second-best faceoff grade among players on losing clubs after Nieuwendyk. 48 points at $1M expiring is below market. ATL at 13-24-2 with 11 expiring are in full rebuild. Fold him into the ATL conversation alongside Kovalchuk/Heatley as a cheaper alternative or add-on.

recommendations.summary: Cammalleri (LA, RW, 22, POTE 98, 27 pts/23 GP at 1.17 pace, $1.10M expiring) is the highest-potential young player on any seller; LA at 13-20-5 with 13 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 98 at age 22 already producing at 1.17 pts/g. Solves the top-six scoring gap for five years. December proposal: Holden plus DET 2nd rounder. Extend to include Frolov if LA will do a double.

recommendations.summary: Frolov (LA, LW, 22, POTE 96, 40 pts/34 GP at 1.18 pace, $1.10M expiring) is on the same LA roster as Cammalleri and fills the left-wing slot in the top six.
recommendations.rationale: 40 points in 34 games at 1.18 pace with POTE 96 and 86 SPEE / 88 SHPW. Same club and same contract year as Cammalleri; a double acquisition fills two top-six spots in one negotiation. Package cost should be assessed jointly, not doubled.

recommendations.summary: Chara (OTT, D, 27, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 45 pts/41 GP, $1.70M expiring) solves the toughness gap on the blueline and is a confirmed seller on OTT (15-21-4, 11 expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Already the anchor of the three-package stack: Belfour + R1 for Chara + Havlat. OTT have deteriorated since the Jan 10 confirmation and remain in rebuild. No change to proposal.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 90 SPEE, 82 ovr, $900K x2 years) is the purest toughness forward available but CHI's profitability and two years left make acceptance uncertain.
recommendations.rationale: The highest TOUG on any roster in the league. CHI are 12-23-6 but profit $24.48M, so they are not forced. Use only if Chara and Abid both stall. Do not spend a first or second rounder.

recommendations.summary: Walker (STL, D, 24, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $500K expiring) is the cheapest impact toughness player in the league; STL are 10-24-3 with 9 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: 95 TOUG and 93 CHKG at $500K. Five points in 33 games means he is purely a checker. A playoff 7th-pair D. Should cost a 5th or late pick. Pick him up regardless of what other deals land.

recommendations.summary: Conroy (CGY, C, 33, 91 FACE, 55 pts/45 GP, $2.00M expiring) is the best balance of faceoffs and production available at a reasonable price; CGY are 14-24-6 with 10 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: 55 points and 91 FACE at $2M expiring. Three years younger than Nieuwendyk at half the salary for one fewer FACE point. If we need a playoff faceoff answer that also scores, he is the pick.

recommendations.summary: Nieuwendyk (FLA, C, 38, 95 FACE, 51 pts/44 GP, $4.10M expiring) is the best faceoff man in the league; FLA at 16-22-4 with 18 expiring are the most expiring-loaded seller in the East.
recommendations.rationale: 95 FACE at 51 pts. Pure rental at 38 and $4.10M. If the plan is to win a series in April rather than build for October, he is the answer. Otherwise Conroy is the same solution cheaper and younger.

recommendations.summary: Bouwmeester (FLA, D, 21, POTE 96, 78 ovr, 18 pts/44 GP, $1.20M expiring) is a franchise blueliner on a club with 18 expiring deals; he is the best long-term defenceman available.
recommendations.rationale: Already playing 44 games at 21 on a 40-point team with 90 SPEE and 85 SHPW. FLA at 16-22-4 with 18 expiring are in full teardown. Would cost a first or second plus a prospect. The highest ceiling among defenceman targets.

recommendations.summary: Thornton (BOS, C, 25, 91 ovr, 82 TOUG, 80 FACE, 66 pts/40 GP, $4.00M expiring) fills toughness and faceoffs simultaneously in one player; Boston at 16-19-4 with 13 expiring are approaching the seller threshold.
recommendations.rationale: The only player in the league who closes two gaps at once. 66 points at 25 with 82 TOUG and 80 FACE. At $4.00M it is the most expensive rental but the most complete answer. Acceptance uncertain — BOS have not hit the .500 threshold yet but are sliding.

recommendations.summary: Kovalchuk (ATL, RW, 21, 92 ovr, 78 pts/41 GP, $1.10M expiring) remains the highest-scoring player available on the most motivated seller (ATL 13-24-2, 11 expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Unchanged from prior findings. ATL binary with Heatley: if they re-sign one, the other is the target. If both stay, the ATL target is dead. Savard provides a cheaper faceoff-first alternative from the same club.

recommendations.summary: Jillson (BOS, D, 24, POTE 94, 80 TOUG, 84 CHKG, 17 pts/43 GP, $1.00M expiring) is a young, tough, fast defenceman on a BOS club sliding toward the seller threshold.
recommendations.rationale: 80 TOUG and 84 CHKG with 86 SPEE at 24 fills the toughness gap from the blue. BOS at 16-19-4 with 13 expiring are 3 games under .500. Cheaper than Chara but a step below in production.

recommendations.proposed: Chara (D, 27, $1.70M, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 45 pts/41 GP, expiring) + Havlat (RW, 23, $0.90M, 61 pts/42 GP, 87 base, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour and the 1st-rounder to Ottawa for Chara and Havlat; converts $6.50M salary into toughness and top-six scoring at a combined $2.60M.
recommendations.rationale: OTT are 15-19-4 with 11 expiring deals; Chara and Havlat walk in July for nothing. Belfour at 91 ovr gives them 20 wins while they develop young goalies, and a 1st-rounder is their best rebuild asset. We shed $3.90M net payroll and solve the toughness gap (73 to 88-89) and add 61-point secondary scoring in one negotiation. Acceptance uncertain because we are asking for two above-75 players for one expiring goalie and one pick.

recommendations.current: Holden (C, 26, $1.20M, 0 GP, 81 ovr, expiring) + TOR 3rd-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Abid (LW, 24, $400K, 87 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 56 pts/44 GP, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Holden and the 3rd-rounder to Pittsburgh for Abid; fills the checking-wing gap and saves $800K.
recommendations.rationale: PIT are 12-21-5 with 14 expiring deals; Abid at $400K walks unless moved. A 3rd-rounder plus Holden (84 ACCE, 83 SHPW, a body for their roster rebuild) is better than zero. We gain a 56-point winger at 87 TOUG for the salary of a 13th forward, solving the coach's top toughness flag. Acceptance likely given PIT's record and roster state.

recommendations.current: Chistov (LW, 21, $1.10M, 11 pts/31 GP, 0.33 pts/g, 95 POTE, expiring) + DET 2nd-round pick
recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov and the DET 2nd-rounder to Atlanta for Kovalchuk; swaps a stalled prospect for the league's highest-scoring available 21-year-old at no net salary change.
recommendations.rationale: ATL are 13-24-2 with 11 expiring deals. Kovalchuk walks unless they re-sign at $5M+ next year. A 1st-round asset (the DET pick) plus a 95-potential 21-year-old is real value for a player they lose anyway. Chistov is unlined and declining at 0.33 pts/g; the coach already flagged Nash over him. If ATL will bundle Savard (89 FACE, $1.00M, 48 pts/43 GP, expiring) into this conversation at no extra cost, take him — he closes the faceoff gap alongside Sundin. Acceptance uncertain on whether ATL prefer to re-sign one of Kovalchuk/Heatley rather than deal.

recommendations.summary: Pick up Walker from St. Louis for a late-round pick before the deadline; playoff insurance at the checking position.
recommendations.rationale: STL are 10-24-3 with 9 expiring deals. Walker at $500K expiring with 95 TOUG and 93 CHKG is absurd value for a playoff-ready seventh blueliner. Costs a 5th or nothing. No reason to pass on this regardless of what else happens.

recommendations.proposed: Savard (C, 27, $1.00M, 89 FACE, 48 pts/43 GP, expiring, ATL)
recommendations.summary: If ATL bundle Savard into the Kovalchuk conversation at no extra cost, accept; if not, he is a separate late target for the 4th-rounder if ATL are still looking to clear by February.
recommendations.rationale: Savard's 89 FACE alongside Sundin solves the three-lines-losing-draws problem. At $1.00M expiring on a 13-24-2 team with 11 expiring deals, ATL will deal him for a pick rather than lose him for nothing. Priority is the Kovalchuk bundle; Savard is a free add-on or a cheap solo target.

recommendations.summary: Chara is the only player in the league who solves the toughness gap with a first-round-calibre defenceman at 27 and an expiring $1.70M.
recommendations.rationale: No TOR player above 73 toughness. Chara reads 88 TOUG and 89 CHKG at 27, expiring, on a 15-19-4 OTT club with 11 expiring deals. The Dec 15 read on OTT was stale; they are confirmed sellers.

recommendations.summary: Bell at 93 TOUG, 24, $0.90M, two years left is the cheap toughness acquisition if Chara's price is too high.
recommendations.rationale: He is young enough to develop with the core, two years of control, and costs a late pick. Falls back to the December package if STL engage on Mogilny.

recommendations.summary: Line Tucker for his 83 CHKG; he is the only internal player who adds a seventh checker.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker at 29 with 83 checking is the only roster option above 82 outside the aging top three. His toughness base is 70, so this patches checking only, not toughness.

recommendations.summary: The faceoff gap is thin with only Sundin at 90 and nobody above 75, but Chlup at 18 and 75 FACE is the internal fix on a one-year horizon.
recommendations.rationale: No trade target is worth a first-rounder for faceoffs alone when Chlup could be 80+ by next March. Monitor his FACE development; if he stalls below 78, open an acquisition in July.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup to a 5-6 year deal now, before a full top-nine season raises his price.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup is 18, $2.34M, two years left, POTE 95, 23 points in 33 games; the cheapest long-term lock on a future star available.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash and Kaberle on 5-6 years and put depth on 2-3 so the $28.6M July wall splits across two summers.
recommendations.rationale: 17 one-year deals worth $28.60M expire together; the manual warns against a roster that renews all at once.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour for a draft pick before March; do not release him in July.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39, $6.50M, one year, CONS 50, and qualifies for the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic, which converts him to a pick.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Aebischer on a 2-3 year deal to make him the crease plan once Belfour moves.
recommendations.rationale: Aebischer is 26, $0.50M, one year; Tellqvist is 25. Without a term, both crease prospects walk with the 17-deal cluster.

recommendations.summary: Use the two first-rounders on young expiring sellers for March, not on old rentals.
recommendations.rationale: Kovalchuk (21, 92 base, expiring) and Chara (27, expiring) are confirmed seller targets; the club holds own round-0 plus a DET round-1 plus R2/R3/R4, enough to fund both and still keep a June pick.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour (39, $6.50M, 91 ovr, expiring) to any club for a draft pick before the March deadline using the above-80-asset mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: He's 39, $6.50M, expiring. Aebischer (26, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV, $0.50M) is ready to start. The above-80-asset mechanic converts him to a pick for free.

recommendations.summary: Lead deadline negotiation for Thornton (91 ovr, 66 pts/40 GP, 25, $4.00M expiring) from BOS at 16-19-3.
recommendations.rationale: BOS is 43 points, 9th in the East, and a confirmed seller. Thornton fills the coach's top-six gap and toughness (82 TOUG) simultaneously. Better than the Jackman package if BOS engages.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Chara (85 base, 45 pts/41 GP, 27, $1.70M expiring) from OTT at 15-21-4 as an alternative or complement to Thornton.
recommendations.rationale: OTT is 40 points, 10th in the East, confirmed seller. Chara's 88 TOUG and 89 CHKG directly address the roster's toughness ceiling of 73. A double acquisition with Thornton in one negotiation is the highest-value deadline outcome.

recommendations.summary: Trade Svehla (D, 36, $3.60M expiring) to a contender for a late pick or depth before March.
recommendations.rationale: 36 years old, $3.60M, expiring. Eminger (21) and Colaiacovo (21) are behind him and ready. Moving him clears salary and opens a top-four spot for the young pair.

recommendations.summary: Trade Roberts (LW, 38, $2.70M expiring) before March; if no taker, let go in July.
recommendations.rationale: 38 years old, $2.70M. The coach already flagged three top-six forwards declining. Nash (0.88 pts/g, 20) is in on the third line over Chistov and is the replacement.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik (RW, 22, $1.10M) on 5-6 years at the start of free agency. This is the most urgent single re-signing.
recommendations.rationale: 22 years old, $1.10M expiring. A star winger on a one-year deal is the biggest summer risk. A 5-6 year deal at any number the game allows is correct.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards (C, 24, $1.00M) on 5-6 years. He is the number-one centre's long-term partner or successor.
recommendations.rationale: 24, $1.00M expiring. A 24-year-old centre on a one-year deal will see his asking price jump after one more season. Lock now at the current number.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash (LW, 20, $1.20M) on 5-6 years before his second full season erases his current price.
recommendations.rationale: 0.88 pts/g at age 20 on $1.20M. If he repeats 40+ points in a full season, his asking price will be 3x current. Lock immediately.

recommendations.summary: Lock Kaberle (D, 26, $1.90M) on 5-6 years as the top-pairing left defenceman.
recommendations.rationale: 26, $1.90M, in his prime. The only top-pair D-man on the roster with a real shot at staying. A 5-6 year deal prevents the next cluster from including the blueline.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger (D, 21, $1.20M) on 4-5 years as a top-four defenceman.
recommendations.rationale: 21 years old, $1.20M. With Svehla leaving, he and Colaiacovo are the future second pair. Lock them both on similar terms.

recommendations.summary: Lock Colaiacovo (D, 21, $1.10M) on 4-5 years after his full-time second-pair season.
recommendations.rationale: 21, $1.10M, averaging 18.5 MPG when dressed. The coach is giving him a full-time spot. Lock him on the same terms as Eminger to stagger against Kaberle.

recommendations.summary: Lock Upshall (RW, 21, $1.20M) on 3 years. Not 5-6 until he proves himself at 12+ MPG.
recommendations.rationale: 0.69 pts/g on 9.7 MPG. The coach wants him up a line. A 3-year deal keeps him cheap through the development window; if he breaks out, extend then.

recommendations.summary: Renew Holden (C, 26, $1.20M) on 2-3 years as third/fourth-line centre.
recommendations.rationale: 26, $1.20M. Reliable depth centre. 2-3 years is cheap and staggers him against Richards.

recommendations.summary: Renew Smirnov (LW, 20, $0.40M) on 2-3 years as cheap fourth-line depth.
recommendations.rationale: 20, $0.40M. Inexpensive young forward. 2-3 years keeps him cheap and off the star cluster.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Chistov (LW, 21, $1.10M, 0.33 pts/g in 27 games). Nash replaces him permanently.
recommendations.rationale: The coach already benched him for Nash. 0.33 pts/g at 21 is not enough to earn a second contract here.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Tellqvist (G, 25, $0.80M). Aebischer starts; Belfour is traded. One backup spot remains but can be filled cheaper.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Renberg (LW, 32, $2.00M). Let him go or include in a deadline trade.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Chara from OTT: 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 82 ovr, 46 pts/43 GP, 28, $1.70M expiring. Single best player on the board; closes toughness and checking in one body.

recommendations.rationale: PIT at 12-21-5 with 14 expiring deals must sell. At $400K he fills toughness and checking while adding 1.26 pts/g. Koltsov is the proposed return per the December finding.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Doan from PHX: 84 ovr, 84 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 39 pts/44 GP, 29, $2.40M expiring. Fills toughness, checking and top-six scoring simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: PHX at 16-23-4 with 14 expiring deals and $13.33M profit are sellers. He is the only player on the board who closes the toughness gap while providing legitimate top-six production.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Komisarek from MTL: 88 CHKG, 81 TOUG, 78 ovr, 92 POTE, 52 pts/43 GP, 23, $1.10M expiring. Fills checking and toughness now with star upside.
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 12-23-4 with 14 expiring deals and $53.20M payroll are under pressure to shed salary. A 23-year-old D-man with 92 potential and 52 points at $1.10M is the best keeper target on the board.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Kovalchuk from ATL: 86 ovr, 80 pts/42 GP, 22, $1.10M expiring, 86 POTE. Highest-scoring player on a confirmed seller.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 13-23-2 with 11 expiring deals cannot retain both him and Heatley. He does not fill toughness but 80 points at 22 is the best scoring addition available. Package: own first-rounder plus Koltsov per December finding.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jackman from STL: 86 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 90 SPD, 79 ovr, 24 pts/42 GP, 24, $0.70M with three years left. A keeper, not a rental.
recommendations.rationale: STL at 9-24-3 are the worst club in the league with 9 expiring deals. Three years at $700K on a 24-year-old with 90 speed and 87 checking is the cheapest long-term toughness addition on the board. Already targeted in the December package.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Belanger from LA: 92 FACE, 69 TOUG, 73 CHKG, 74 ovr, 28, $0.70M expiring. Cheapest path to a second elite draw man.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 13-19-5 with 13 expiring deals are sellers. His scoring is minimal (9 pts/43 GP) but he wins 92-calibre draws and is physical, which is exactly the second-centre profile Sundin needs behind him.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell from CHI: 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 78 ovr, 25, $0.90M with two years left. A keeper who closes the toughness gap permanently.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 11-23-6 with 10 expiring deals are sellers, but profitable at $24.96M so acceptance is uncertain. Two years at $900K means he stays past the deadline, unlike Chara or Doan.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Cammalleri from LA: 79 ovr, 98 POTE, 26 pts/22 GP, 23, $1.10M expiring. Highest potential on the board at 1.18 pts/g pace.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 13-19-5 cannot keep him. His health is the risk: 22 games played suggests an injury. If he is healthy, a 23-year-old with 98 potential is a franchise player.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bouwmeester from FLA: 77 ovr, 96 POTE, 89 SPD, 82 CHKG, 31 MPG at 22, $1.20M expiring. A keeper defenceman with elite upside.
recommendations.rationale: FLA carry 18 expiring deals, the most in the league, at 16-22-3. They must sell. A 22-year-old already logging 31 minutes with 96 potential is a franchise blueliner if developed.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Sturm from SJ: 84 ovr, 61 pts/44 GP, 27, $1.00M expiring. Top-six scoring on a confirmed seller.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 16-20-5 with 14 expiring deals are in sell mode. He does not fill toughness but 61 points at $1M at age 27 is efficient value if they engage.

recommendations.proposed: Chara (D, 28, $1.70M expiring, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 82 ovr, 46 pts/43 GP) + Havlat (LW, 24, $900K expiring, 86 ovr, 61 pts/43 GP)

The first-rounder is their path to a franchise player. We get the best player on the board (Chara, 90/91 toughness/checking, 46 pts) plus a 61-point winger, and the net payroll drop from $6.50M to $2.60M helps the July renewal wall.

recommendations.summary: Give the DET second-rounder plus Chistov to ATL for Kovalchuk; 80 points from a 22-year-old at $1.10M for the rental window.

They keep Heatley (base 91 vs 89) and rebuild with a 21-year-old prospect (95 POTE, 89 SPEE) plus a second-rounder. Kovalchuk walks in July for nothing if they try to retain both. The coach is already benching Chistov behind Nash. If ATL re-signs Kovalchuk the target is dead.

recommendations.proposed: Abid (LW, 25, $400K expiring, 86 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 77 ovr, 54 pts/43 GP)

Abid gives toughness (86/86) and secondary scoring at a fraction of Chara's cost. Holden has not played a single game this season and is expiring.

recommendations.rationale: No internal player is within 15 points of 80 in faceoffs. Avery's 88 TOUG also lifts the toughness ceiling from 73 to 88. LA at 9-16-5 with 13 expiring deals has no reason to keep a fourth-centre specialist.

recommendations.summary: Line Tucker (83 CHKG) to raise the 80+ checking count from six to seven without any trade.

recommendations.summary: Confirm whether Kaberle (26, 97 ENDU, 90 CLCH) is genuinely unlined; if so, the coach must put him on a pair.

recommendations.summary: Scoring depth is not a gap: 13 players at 80+ with the age transition (Mogilny 35, Roberts 38 to Gaborik 22, Richards 24, Afinogenov 25) already in motion.
recommendations.rationale: The succession is on the roster and carrying 80+ grades today. No acquisition needed here; Chlup's extension and Spacek's ice time handle the next tier.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup on a 5-6 year deal at his current $2.34M price before a full top-nine season erases the rookie-window number.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup is 18, POTE 95, 23 pts in 32 games, $2.34M with two years left. His next contract is the cheapest star deal on the roster if done now and the most expensive if done after another season.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour before March for a draft pick using the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic; removes $6.50M and opens the crease for Aebischer and Tellqvist.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39, $6.50M expiring, CONS 50. Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, 19 starts) is ready. Trading Belfour now avoids a July re-signing at a reduced rate or losing him for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Begin the summer stagger by locking Gaborik (22, 62 pts, POTE 90), Richards (24, 46 pts, POTE 88) and Nash (20, 30 pts, POTE 95) on 5-6 year deals this month.
recommendations.rationale: All three are in the 17-player $28.6M July cluster. Locking them now at current prices ($1.10M, $1.00M, $1.20M) prevents a summer where the whole core renews at once and prices spike together.

recommendations.summary: The 30-33 bridge is thin (only Sundin, Salo, Renberg) but the 24-29 group locked on 4-year deals (Afinogenov, Fischer, McCabe, Pilar) is the real bridge and does not need outside help.
recommendations.rationale: Afinogenov is 25 POTE 95, Fischer 24 POTE 90, Pilar 27 POTE 88, all on 4 years. They will be 28-31 in 2007-08, which is the bridge the club needs without acquiring it.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour for a draft pick before the March deadline using the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic; do not release him in July.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39, $6.50M, 91 overall and expiring; the mechanic turns him into a pick while he still carries 80+ value, and Aebischer (26, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV) already covers the net.

recommendations.summary: Lead with Kovalchuk as the deadline buy: own first-rounder plus Koltsov to ATL.
recommendations.rationale: Kovalchuk is 21, 92 overall, 69 pts in 38 GP on $1.10M expiring at a seller outside the Eastern top ten; a young keeper, not a rental, filling the third top-six slot the coach says is declining.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Chara from OTT before March for a young keeper and first/second-round capital.

recommendations.summary: Keep the December package as the deadline fallback: execute Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton if Kovalchuk and Chara are dead by late February.
recommendations.rationale: The package is unexecuted, costs the own first-rounder nothing, and fills the coach's toughness (to ~90) and faceoff (96 beside Sundin's 90) gaps; don't waste the deadline if the value targets fail.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik (22), Richards (24), Nash (20) and Kaberle (26) on 5-6 year deals now at their current salaries.
recommendations.rationale: These four are the young core in the same $28.6M July cluster; signing stars to 5-6 years now freezes the rookie-window price and avoids the yearly re-up that ratchets demands.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup (18, $2.34M, two years left, POTE 95, 20 pts in 26 GP) to 5-6 years before a full top-nine season erases his rookie price.
recommendations.rationale: Not expiring this summer but the most urgent single contract on the roster; the extension is cheap now and expensive after one breakout year.

recommendations.summary: Lock the 21-year-olds Colaiacovo (18.5 MPG when dressed), Eminger and Upshall on 3-5 years to get them past restricted status.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla (36, $3.60M), Roberts (38, $2.70M) and Renberg (32, $2.00M) for a pick or cheap prospect before March; otherwise release at season end.

recommendations.proposed: move for Spacek or let walk
recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov (21, $1.10M, 0.33 pts/g in 27 GP) for Spacek (19, 0.61 pts/g in 23 GP) as the coach wants, or let him walk.

recommendations.summary: If Chara is unavailable, take Brad Stuart (87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 25, $1.80M expiring, 35 pts/42 GP) from SJ.

recommendations.summary: Take Belanger (97 FACE, 82 base, 27, $0.70M expiring) from LA on a late-round pick for the playoffs.
recommendations.rationale: 97 FACE is the highest in the league and solves the one-man faceoff problem for this spring. 9 pts/42 GP is fine for a 4C. LA at 13-18-5 with 13 expiring will not keep him. Cheapest gap-fill available.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Avery (83 TOUG, 93 FACE, 79 base, 24, $0.40M, 2yr) from LA to fill toughness and faceoffs at $0.40M.
recommendations.rationale: Fills both gaps simultaneously at the lowest salary on the board. 5 pts/42 GP is poor but his role is draws and physical play. LA at 13-18-5 will not fight for a 4C. Two years left is a slight complication versus Belanger.

recommendations.summary: Trade for Komisarek (77 base, POTE 91, 52 pts/42 GP, 23, $1.10M expiring) from MTL and lock on 5 years.

recommendations.summary: Rent Conroy (94 FACE, 85 base, 51 pts/42 GP, 33, $2.00M expiring) from CGY for the playoff run.
recommendations.rationale: Solves the faceoff problem for April while Chlup (18, FACE 75, POTE 95) develops. CGY at 13-22-6 with 10 expiring will move him. A second-rounder or DET pick gets him. One-year answer only.

recommendations.summary: Execute the December package leg for Sillinger (91 FACE, 86 base, $1.80M expiring) from PHX with a third-rounder.

recommendations.rationale: 89 TOUG closes the toughness gap outright. 80 base on $0.70M with 3 years left is a keeper, not a rental. STL at 9-23-3 with 9 expiring are in rebuild. Mogilny (35, $3.60M expiring) is the salary STL can use for cap space elsewhere.

recommendations.rationale: 22 years old, 61 points in 42 games, $1.10M expiring. He is the highest-output player on a one-year deal. A free-agent scramble across 17 simultaneous renewals risks losing him or paying a premium.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on 5-6 years the moment July opens.
recommendations.rationale: 24 years old, 46 points in 42 games, $1.00M expiring. Top-nine centre, prime age, the cheapest high-output forward on the roster. Lock him alongside Gaborik.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on 5 years at July. Upshall and Alexeev on 3-4 years.
recommendations.rationale: Nash is 20 with 30 points in 34 games and $1.20M expiring. Upshall is 21 with 17 points and POTE 99. Both are the second wave; stagger them one tier behind Gaborik and Richards so no single summer carries every negotiation.

recommendations.summary: Let Svehla ($3.60M, 36), Roberts ($2.70M, 38) and Renberg ($2.00M, 32) walk at expiry.
recommendations.rationale: $8.30M in salary relief from players aged 32-38 with declining production. The roster has 25 players at 29 or younger; these three are surplus to the shape.

recommendations.summary: No payroll concern. $66.97M against $68.54M revenue and $27.98M profit leaves room for the re-signing wave.
recommendations.rationale: Even a 50% raise on the $12.80M young-core cluster adds roughly $6M against a club already clearing $28M in profit. The constraint is the number of negotiations, not the dollars.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour (39, 91 ovr, $6.50M, expiring) at the March deadline for a draft pick using the above-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Aebischer (26, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV, 19 starts) is ready for the number-one role. Belfour is a free pick if moved before July.

recommendations.summary: Trade Svehla (36, 85 base, $3.60M, expiring) at the March deadline for a draft pick.
recommendations.rationale: Qualifies for the above-80 expiring mechanic. Colaiacovo (21) and Eminger (21) are ready for the second pair minutes.

recommendations.summary: Trade Roberts (38, 87 base, $2.70M, expiring) at the March deadline for a draft pick.
recommendations.rationale: Third above-80 expiring asset on this roster. Jackman and Sillinger from the December package cover the top-nine minutes he plays.

recommendations.summary: Execute the December 22 three-deal package in February: Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton.
recommendations.rationale: Fills toughness from 73 to 90 and faceoffs with a 96 man. Does not spend the first-rounder. Agreed 22 Dec, not yet executed as of Jan 8.

recommendations.summary: If ATL remains below .500 in February, offer own first-rounder plus Koltsov for Kovalchuk (21, 92 ovr, 69 pts in 38 GP, $1.10M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Highest-scoring available player on the most motivated seller. Acceptance uncertain; the AI has not been observed accepting a 92-overall player for a first and a 69-overall.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik (22, 96/91, $1.10M) to 5-6 years in July.
recommendations.rationale: Highest-rated player on the roster at age 22. Annual renewal ratchets his demands every year.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards (24, 85/82, $1.00M) to 5-6 years in July.
recommendations.rationale: Centre of the future top six at 24 on a $1.00M deal. Lock the price now.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash (20, 81/77, $1.20M) to 5-6 years in July.
recommendations.rationale: 0.88 pts/g at age 20. The coach is putting him on the third line now; he will price up fast.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle (26, 82/84, $1.90M) to 5 years in July.
recommendations.rationale: Best defenceman on the roster at 26. Five years is the star standard.

recommendations.summary: Sign Aebischer (26, $0.50M) to 2-3 years before July.
recommendations.rationale: 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV in 19 starts. The next number one. Cheap now, will price up after Belfour leaves and he starts 60+ games.

recommendations.summary: Sign Upshall (21, 77/78, $1.20M) to 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: 0.69 pts/g on 9.7 MPG with the coach asking for 12+. Short deal keeps flexibility if he stalls.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger (21, 75/76, $1.20M) to 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: Young blueliner behind Colaiacovo on the depth chart. Short deal until he proves he is a top-four D.

recommendations.summary: Sign Colaiacovo (21, 71/72, $1.10M) to 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: Coach wants him on the second pair full-time. He will price up after a season of 20+ MPG.

recommendations.summary: Sign Alexeev (23, 76/76, $1.10M) to 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: 23-year-old depth forward. Short deal keeps the roster flexible while younger players emerge.

recommendations.summary: Sign Holden (26, 75/76, $1.20M) to 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: 26-year-old bottom-six centre. Short deal; he is depth not a long-term piece.

recommendations.summary: Sign Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) to 1-2 years as backup behind Aebischer.
recommendations.rationale: With Belfour traded and Aebischer starting, Tellqvist is the insurance goalie. Cheap 1-year deal.

recommendations.summary: Let Renberg (32, $2.00M, 77/80) walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: 32 years old, $2.00M, below 80 overall. Does not qualify for the above-80 pick mechanic and is not in the timeline.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov (20, 50/51, $0.40M) expires in July. No action now; decide in June whether a 2-year development deal is worth a roster spot.
recommendations.rationale: At 50 overall he is not a player anyone trades for or re-signs in March. Low urgency.

recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov (21, 80/78, $1.10M, expiring) at the deadline or let him walk. Do not let him sit all season.
recommendations.rationale: 0.33 pts/g in 27 games, Nash replaces him on the third line. If he plays 6 games the rest of the season he leaves for nothing; trade for something.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Kovalchuk (ATL, 86 ovr, POTE 97, 21, $1.10M expiring, 77 pts/40 GP) before ATL re-sign him; own first-rounder plus Koltsov.
recommendations.rationale: The highest-rated player on the board, on the most motivated seller (ATL 13-21-2, 11 expiring, $36.79M payroll). He fills Mogilny's slot and is 15 years younger.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Thornton (BOS, 91 ovr, 82 TOUG, 80 FACE, 91 SPEE, 25, $4.00M UFA, 66 pts/40 GP); the Jan 5 dismissal was based on wrong stats. DET first plus a depth body.
recommendations.rationale: Solves faceoffs, toughness, and top-six centre depth in one player. BOS are 15-19-3 with 13 expiring. At $4.00M for a rental the cost is high, but the grades fix three gaps at once.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Drury (BUF, 86 ovr, 85 FACE, 73 TOUG, 88 SPEE, 28, $2.00M expiring, 59 pts/40 GP); fills faceoffs, toughness, and scoring in one body.
recommendations.rationale: 1.48 pts/g at 28 on a 16-16-3 club with 10 expiring. Cheaper than Thornton at $2.00M and fills all three gaps. Competes with Kovalchuk for the same pick.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Chara (OTT, D, 80 ovr, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 82 SPEE, 27, $1.70M expiring, 45 pts/41 GP); the Jan 5 read that OTT were not sellers was wrong.
recommendations.rationale: 45 points from the blueline with 88/89 toughness-checking. OTT are 15-19-4 (.441) with 11 expiring, which is a rebuild. Price should be a second-rounder plus a depth forward.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell (CHI, LW, 78 ovr, 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 86 SPEE, 24, $0.90M, 2yr) as the pure toughness answer.
recommendations.rationale: 91 TOUG and 89 CHKG at 24 with 2 years remaining, on the worst team in the West (11-22-6). Only 15 points in 41 games but the two-way grades are exactly what Toronto lacks. Two years left means this is a keeper, not a rental.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Abid (PIT, LW, 74 ovr, POTE 94, 83 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 24, $0.40M expiring, 53 pts/42 GP) if Kovalchuk and Drury are unavailable or too expensive.
recommendations.rationale: 53 points at $0.40M from a 12-21-5 club with 14 expiring. Toughness and checking alongside the scoring. Koltsov or Safronov is the return.

recommendations.summary: Execute the December package for Sillinger (PHX, C, 88 ovr, 96 FACE, 33, $1.80M expiring, 27 pts/26 GP); PHX at 15-22-4 with 14 expiring are sellers.
recommendations.rationale: 96 FACE is the only answer to a one-deep faceoff group. The package (R3 only) is already agreed. Execute it before the market shifts.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Avery (LA, C, 73 ovr, 90 FACE, 79 TOUG, 84 CHKG, 24, $0.40M, 2yr) for a late-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: Faceoffs, toughness, and checking at $0.40M with 2 years remaining. Only 5 points in 41 games so he is a specialist, not a top-six piece. LA have 13 expiring and no reason to retain him.

recommendations.summary: Consider Samsonov (BOS, LW, 87 ovr, 75 pts/40 GP, 26, $1.90M expiring) as a cheaper alternative to Thornton if BOS will move both.
recommendations.rationale: 87 overall at 26 with 1.88 pts/g on a 15-19-3 club with 13 expiring. $1.90M is a third of Thornton's salary for 9 points less. Fills the left-wing slot directly.

recommendations.summary: If ATL are rebuilding, ask whether Kovalchuk and Heatley (ATL, RW, 84 ovr, 73 pts/37 GP, 23, $1.10M expiring) are available as a package.
recommendations.rationale: Both are expiring, both are young (21 and 23), and ATL at 13-21-2 with 11 expiring are the most motivated seller. Two first-rounders plus two prospects clears their top two scorers.

recommendations.summary: Consider Havlat (OTT, LW, 84 ovr, 60 pts/41 GP, 23, $0.90M expiring, SPEE 99) if Chara or another OTT piece is moved.
recommendations.rationale: 60 points at $0.90M, 23 years old, on the same selling club as Chara. Could be bundled in a two-player deal with OTT to reduce total cost.

recommendations.summary: Sturm (SJ, LW, 82 ovr, 56 pts/41 GP, 26, $1.00M expiring) as a winger rental from a 15-19-4 club with 14 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: 56 points at $1.00M at 26 years old. SJ have 14 expiring deals, the second-most in the league. A second-rounder should suffice.

recommendations.current: Koltsov ($1.10M, LW, 23, POTE 94) + DET first-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 86 ovr, POTE 97, 21, $1.10M expiring, 77 pts/40 GP)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Kovalchuk from ATL for the DET first-rounder plus Koltsov; this fills the top-end scoring gap and builds the succession plan around a 21-year-old with POTE 97.
recommendations.rationale: ATL are 13-21-2 with 11 expiring deals and the cheapest payroll ($36.79M). Kovalchuk walks in July unless they re-sign. A first-rounder plus a 23-year-old with POTE 94 and two years of control is textbook rebuild capital. Payroll nets to zero. Acceptance uncertain; if ATL re-sign him before March the target is dead.

recommendations.current: Mogilny ($5.50M, RW, 35) + TOR R2 to STL; TOR R3 to PHX; Safronov ($0.90M, D, 23) + TOR R4 to ATL
recommendations.proposed: Jackman (STL, D, 83 ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, $0.70M, 3yr); Sillinger (PHX, C, 88 ovr, 96 FACE, 33, $1.80M expiring, 27 pts/26 GP); Sutton (ATL, D, 76 ovr, 92 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 27, $1.34M, 4yr)
recommendations.summary: Execute the three-deal package agreed 22 December: fills toughness (73 to 90/92) and faceoffs (90 to 96) in one motion, net payroll drops $2.56M.
recommendations.rationale: STL at 8-17-2 need a veteran scorer for a rebuild and Mogilny still posts 51 pts in 38 GP. PHX at 15-22-4 with 14 expiring have no reason to keep a 33-year-old on an expiring deal. ATL at 13-21-2 are rebuilding around Bouwmeester and Sutton is surplus. All three clubs are well below .500 with heavy expiring deals. Acceptance uncertain on each leg independently.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour to a contender for a draft pick before March, freeing $6.50M and handing the crease to Aebischer without waiting until July.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour qualifies for the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic: any player above 80 on an expiring deal trades for a pick. Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, .898 SV in 19 starts) is the successor. A contender missing a backup goalie absorbs $6.50M for one month of playoffs and a pick. Do this independently of the other proposals.

recommendations.summary: Nash goes in on the third line over Chistov; Nash has 0.88 pts/g at 20 and is sitting, Chistov has 0.33 pts/g in 27 games.
recommendations.rationale: Nash's 30 points in 34 games is a top-six rate from a 20-year-old who keeps getting scratched. Chistov's 0.33 pts/g does not earn a roster spot over that.

recommendations.summary: Move Spezza up to third-line centre from the fourth line to get him above 12 MPG; Chlup shifts to fourth or centres the fourth.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza needs 12+ MPG at 21 with POTE 99 and a climbing rate (0.62 recent). At 8.4 MPG on the fourth line he is stalling. Chlup at 18 can handle fourth-line minutes and still develop.

recommendations.summary: Give Colaiacovo a full-time spot on the second pair; he is averaging 18.5 MPG when dressed and should be in every night.
recommendations.rationale: Colaiacovo at 21, POTE 99, playing 49% of games while Svehla fades and Fischer is structurally broken. The blue line needs him in and the development case is overwhelming.

recommendations.summary: Safronov at 23 with 3 games and 0 points this season cannot develop sitting. Dress him or move him; a decision is overdue.
recommendations.rationale: Three games at 13.7 MPG with zero production is not a player being developed. The GM said to keep this in front of him; it is still in front of him and the window is closing.

recommendations.summary: Spacek at 19 with 0.61 pts/g in 23 games has earned a dressed spot; he should replace Koltsov or Chistov if either is dropped.
recommendations.rationale: 0.61 pts/g at 19 is better than what Chistov (0.33) and possibly Koltsov (unverifiable recent rate) are providing. Spacek should be next in if a spot opens.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 12+ MPG or tell the GM to accept he stagnates at 6-7.
recommendations.rationale: Rate climbing (0.43→0.56) while minutes fell (9.1→6.7). At 21 he needs 12+ to consolidate. The trend is getting worse, not better.

recommendations.summary: Move Upshall up a line. He's at 0.69 pts/g on 9.7 MPG and has earned 12+.
recommendations.rationale: Rate doubled from 0.33 to 0.69 while minutes dropped from 13.4 to 9.7. Producing top-six rate on bottom-six ice.

recommendations.summary: Three top-six forwards all declining simultaneously. Start planning the post-35 top six now.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 1.46→1.00, Mogilny 1.62→0.92, Roberts 1.29→1.06. All three aging at once. Richards and Gaborik can absorb the shift but we need a third option emerging.

recommendations.current: Chlup, Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Colaiacovo
recommendations.summary: Six young players all climbing on both rate and minutes. Leave them alone.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 0.62→0.82, Gaborik 1.42→1.59, Richards 1.08→1.18, Nash 0.83→1.00, Eminger 0.35→1.25, Colaiacovo 0.44→0.64. All ascending. Do not disrupt.

recommendations.summary: Move Spezza to third-line centre and slide Koltsov to wing; Spezza goes from 8.4 to 11-13 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 89 (down 4) on 8.4 MPG is below even the 70s band of 10; his 0.47 pts/g and climbing rate demand more ice. Koltsov at 96 on 10.0 MPG is comfortable and can absorb a wing role.

recommendations.summary: Give Sundin the closest thing to 20 MPG the lines allow; he's at 17.3 with 90+ calibre and morale dropping 4.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 1.27 pts/g expects 20 minutes per the morale model; at 17.3 he's 2.7 short and losing 4 morale. Every minute reclaimed for him is worth more than the marginal shift on Gaborik or Richards who are at their bands.

recommendations.summary: Safronov's morale is cracking (down 5 to 95) after 3 games; the GM needs to dress him or tell him he's not in the plan.
recommendations.rationale: A 23-year-old with a 95 grade and 13.7 MPG in 3 appearances is a wasted asset whose unhappiness is now showing. No line change fixes a player who isn't being dressed.

recommendations.summary: Aebischer at 81 morale after 19 starts and a benching is the GM's to solve; trade or accept the situation.
recommendations.rationale: 81 morale is the lowest on the roster and the only fix for a scratched goalie is more starts or a new team. Neither is in the coach's hands.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger to the first pair with McCabe; drop Fischer to the second pair with Svehla.
recommendations.rationale: Eminger at 1.00 pts/g and McCabe at 84 checking give us the only first-pair combo on this roster. Fischer at 0.15 pts/g has failed the role for 13+ games and Svehla at 0.40 pts/g is done as a top-pair D.

recommendations.proposed: Roberts, McCabe, Fischer (three-man) or dress Tucker as fourth
recommendations.summary: Remove Mogilny from K1; he is a scoring winger killing penalties with no checking identity.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny at 92 scoring belongs on the power play, not the kill. Roberts, McCabe, and Fischer give a three-man kill with checking means above 80 individually. Tucker at 81 checking is the natural fourth if we dress him.

recommendations.summary: Roster needs a faceoff centre at 80+ to win draws on a second line.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 89 is the only player on the roster who wins draws. Chlup 78, Richards 75, L4 maxes at 55. We lose the faceoff on three lines every game, forcing our D into coverage they should not face. This cannot be solved by lineup arrangement.

recommendations.summary: We have one shutdown unit (L1) and no second option if it is matched out or exhausted.
recommendations.rationale: All three 80+ checkers (McCabe 84, Fischer 84, Roberts 83) are on L1 together. No other combination reaches a checking mean of 75. Against a physical team in a series, if L1 is pinned, we have no answer. Tucker at 81 is scratched and is the closest available option.

recommendations.summary: L2 is built correctly as an offensive line: Gaborik, Afinogenov, Richards.
recommendations.rationale: Speed mean 91, playmaking mean 87, Gaborik at 99/98. Their job is to score and they are suited to it. Checking mean 72 is a trade-off inherent to a fast scoring line.

recommendations.summary: No even-strength or PP line changes for this game.
recommendations.rationale: We are 3-0-0 vs PIT outscoring them 18-8. Their PP is 13.0% on 92 chances, their top D-pair is OVR 76/77, and their only real threat is 39-year-old Lemieux whom our first line matches skill-for-skill. Their faceoff centres (FACE 68, 64) lose to ours (FACE 89, 75) on the top two pairs.

recommendations.summary: Put Chlup on the second penalty kill for this game only; Chistov stays on the third line at even strength.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup is 18 with CHKG 73 and needs NHL PK reps. Their PP converts at 13.0% (12 of 92), so the downside of a rookie mistake is minimal. This is a development exposure, not a matchup adjustment.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour.
recommendations.rationale: OVR 93 against a 2.90 GPG team with a 13.0% PP. This is the easiest start available and he is 39; use these games for wins, not rest.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Chara (84 ovr, 92 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 27, $1.70M expiring) as the deadline target for toughness, which has no internal fix above 73.
recommendations.rationale: The highest base TOUG on the roster is 73. Tucker's 92 reading was a form spike over a 70 base. Chara is the only available player at 90+ TOUG who also fills the checking gap at 93 CHKG. Ottawa at 13 expiring contracts is a motivated seller.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Avery (77 ovr, 94 FACE, 88 TOUG, 29, $0.40M, 2yr) for a late-round pick to fix faceoffs and toughness in one body.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 90 FACE is the only 80+ option and he is 33. Avery is 94 FACE and 88 TOUG at $0.40M on a seller in LA at 9-16-5. He covers two uncovered roles simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Line Tucker on the third unit; his 83 CHKG is the roster's third-best checking grade and he is currently unlined.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker at 83 CHKG and 29 years old is the best young checker available and the coach himself flagged this on Jan 5. Koltsov's checking contribution is zero compared to Tucker's.

recommendations.summary: Give Spacek (84 playmaking, 19) regular top-nine minutes; he is currently not lined despite having the roster's sixth-best playmaking grade.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek at 84 playmaking and 19 years old is the heir to Sundin at centre. The coach flagged his minutes dropping from 16.0 to 10.2 while his rate rose to 0.67. The roster's faceoff depth requires a second centre to emerge.

recommendations.summary: Salo (88 scoring, 30) is on the roster unlined; the coach should dress him if any of the 13 top scorers sit.
recommendations.rationale: 88 scoring is the roster's fifth-best and Salo is 30 — old enough to help now. He is currently contributing zero by not being dressed.

recommendations.summary: Tellqvist (GSH_ 80, REBC 64, INTE 66) is not adequate as a backup next season when Belfour departs and Aebischer moves up.
recommendations.rationale: If Aebischer starts, Toronto needs a 70+ overall backup. Tellqvist's 64 REBC and 66 INTE are replacement-level. Either develop him or target a 30th-round backup at the deadline or next draft.

recommendations.summary: No action needed on speed (25 at 80+), clutch (8 at 80+), or durability (Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92 both under 25). These roles are covered and young.
recommendations.rationale: The roster's strength is speed and clutch. Gaborik at 98 speed and 22 years old anchors this for a decade. No trade should weaken these groups.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup to 5-6 years at $2.5-3.0M before his rookie-window price erases.
recommendations.rationale: He is 18, $2.34M, two years left, POTE 95, 22 points in 30 games. Every top-nine season raises his re-signing cost.

recommendations.summary: Offer Gaborik a 5-6 year extension now at $3.5-4.5M annually.
recommendations.rationale: 61 points in 41 games at $1.10M on an expiring deal is the largest value gap on the roster. Market rate is 3-4x his current salary.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards (46 pts, POTE 88) and Nash (30 pts, POTE 95) on 5-year deals to split the July cluster.
recommendations.rationale: Both are on $1.00-1.20M expiring deals producing 30-46 points. Re-signing them this winter removes $2.20M of expiring risk and keeps the top six intact.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour for a draft pick before March using the above-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: 39 years old, $6.50M expiring, CONS 50, and Aebischer (26, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV, $0.50M) is ready. After July he is gone for zero.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger (POTE 99) and Colaiacovo (POTE 99) on 5-year deals this winter.
recommendations.rationale: Both are 21, on $1.10-1.20M expiring deals, and POTE 99. Their production now is modest (18 pts and 11 pts) but the potential is the highest on the roster. Waiting until they score 40 makes them expensive.

recommendations.summary: Let Svehla walk or trade his expiring year; do not re-sign at $3.60M.
recommendations.rationale: 36, $3.60M, 16 points in 25 games. Eminger, Fischer, and Klesla provide the next wave at POTE 90+ for $0.90-1.20M.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Joe Thornton at the March deadline using Mogilny (87/90) plus a first-round pick as the package.
recommendations.rationale: Thornton at 92 overall fills the centre hole the coach flagged while Sundin fades. He is expiring on a seller, and the price is steep — Mogilny plus a first — so acceptance is uncertain, but a 92-centre changes playoff matchups in ways a pick does not.

recommendations.proposed: Zdeno Chara (82 ovr / 85 base, D, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Pursue Zdeno Chara at the March deadline for a second-round pick or depth plus a pick.
recommendations.rationale: Chara at 85 base overall from a sub-.500 club fills the defensive end of the toughness gap (team average 73). He is a separate deal from Thornton and cheaper at 82 overall.

recommendations.proposed: Trade for a draft pick before March
recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour before March for a draft pick using the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39, $6.50M, and expiring with a 91 overall that qualifies for the above-80 mechanic. Moving him clears the single largest salary on the roster and hands a contender a backup. Aebischer takes over the starting role.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla before March for a late-round pick, or release him in July.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla at 36 and $3.60M is not a playoff piece. Moving him clears money that buys nothing in June.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts before March for a late-round pick, or release him in July.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts at 38 and $2.70M is another old contract with no re-signing path. Clear it with Svehla to remove $6.30M of dead money.

recommendations.proposed: Trade for a pick if above 80 overall, otherwise release
recommendations.summary: If Renberg clears 80 overall, move him before March for a pick; otherwise release in July.
recommendations.rationale: At 32 and $2.00M Renberg is depth we will not re-sign. The above-80 expiring mechanic may apply; if not, the savings are the same whether he walks in March or July.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal before July.
recommendations.rationale: The cheapest star on the roster at 22 and $1.10M. Lock the franchise winger before a 40-goal season triples his price.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on a 5-6 year deal before July.
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old at $1.20M, coach wants him top-nine now. His price rises the moment he produces. Lock at the rookie number.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on a 5 year deal before July.
recommendations.rationale: Cheapest starter on the roster at 24 and $1.00M. Five years is the right term — not six, because his ceiling as a first-line centre is still being assessed.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on a 5 year deal before July.
recommendations.rationale: Top offensive defenceman, most expensive young-core renewal at $1.90M. Five years is the right term at 26.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on a 5-6 year deal before July.
recommendations.rationale: Coach wants him on the first pair now. A first-pair defenceman at 21 with a $1.20M expiring deal is the kind of contract that does not exist next July.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo on a 5-6 year deal before July.
recommendations.rationale: Same case as Eminger: first-pair minutes, 21 years old, expiring rookie salary. Lock him before the price changes.

recommendations.summary: Sign Upshall (21), Chistov (21), Smirnov (20) and Holden (26) on 2-3 year deals, not 5-6, to split the renewal cluster.
recommendations.rationale: These four carry $3.90M combined and are depth players whose long-term role is not yet proven. Two-year deals push their next renewal to 2007, splitting the $25.6M cluster across two summers.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Alexeev. Let him walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: His rate fell from 0.62 to 0.50 and his ice from 11.1 to 7.1 MPG. Five young wingers are ahead of him with no top-nine path.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup on a 5-6 year deal before July, not at renewal.
recommendations.rationale: His $2.34M exists only because of the rookie window. A full top-nine season at 19 erases that price. 20 points in 26 games at 18 already shows the window is closing.

recommendations.summary: Execute the December 22 three-deal package before adding any new targets; it fills toughness and faceoffs without spending the own first-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: Sutton brings 94 TOUG and 90 CHKG at 27 for Safronov+R4, Sillinger gives 91 FACE for R3, Jackman adds toughness for Mogilny+R2. Together they take our best base TOUG from 73 to above 90.

recommendations.summary: If spending the own first-rounder at March, Doan fills toughness (88 TOUG) and checking (93 CHKG) simultaneously while scoring 38 points.
recommendations.rationale: 84 ovr, $2.40M, 28 years, 1 year left. PHX at 15-21-4 with seven expiring deals and $15.08M profit are sellers. He's a re-sign candidate, not a rental.

recommendations.summary: Avery fills faceoffs (93 FACE) and toughness (88 TOUG) for a late-round pick; LA at 13-16-5 has 13 expiring deals and no reason to keep a 4C.
recommendations.rationale: 24 years, $0.40M, 2 years of control. Only 5 points in 40 games but the role is a defensive centre with a strong draw. Highest value-per-pick on the board.

recommendations.summary: If STL eats $3-4M of his $9.50M, Pronger (86 ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 27 pts from D) is the best single defenceman available; if not, skip.
recommendations.rationale: STL at 8-23-3, $56.63M payroll must shed salary. Our payroll rises to $76.47M without relief, cutting profit to ~$17M. Acceptance depends entirely on STL eating salary.

recommendations.summary: Chara at 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 45 pts, 27 years, $1.70M is the best package if OTT engages, but confidence on a seller's market call is low.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 15-18-4 with $27.84M profit are not desperate. The Jan 5 note flagged them as non-sellers. His overall moved from 78 to 82 since then but the club profile hasn't changed.

recommendations.summary: Komisarek (74 ovr, POTE 91, 49 pts in 40 GP from D, 22 years, $1.10M) on a desperate MTL side is a second-rounder development steal.
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 11-22-4 with 14 expiring deals and $53.20M payroll must sell. 1.23 pts/g from a 22-year-old blueliner with 91 potential is the best young-D value on the board.

recommendations.summary: Leclaire (88 ovr, POTE 93, 20 starts, 22 years, $1.10M) is the goalie to acquire in the offseason when Aebischer takes the crease.
recommendations.rationale: CBJ at 14-17-2 have eight expiring deals but $14.74M profit so they won't dump cheap. A later first or early second should get him. This is not a March target.

recommendations.summary: Ference (75 ovr, 86 TOUG, 86 CHKG, $1.20M, 25 years) adds seventh-defenceman toughness for a fourth-rounder; PHX is selling.
recommendations.rationale: One more body above 80 TOUG costs almost nothing and gives the coach a real option for a physical lineup slot.

recommendations.summary: Do not spend the own first on Kovalchuk (91 ovr, 73 pts/39 GP, 21 years); he fills no gap and Doan fills two for the same price.
recommendations.rationale: We lead the league in points and have 13 men at 80+ scoring. Toughness is at zero above 73. The first-rounder should go to the need, not the name.

recommendations.summary: Re-probe Bell (80 ovr, 93 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 24, $0.90M, 2yr) in February if the December package stalls; CHI at 10-22-6 are desperate but profitable.
recommendations.rationale: CHI's $23.92M profit means they aren't financially forced to sell, so acceptance is uncertain. But at the worst record in the league with Fleury and Zhamnov both expiring, their timeline is shifting.

recommendations.proposed: Jackman (83 ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, $0.70M, 3yr) from STL; Sillinger (88 ovr, 91 FACE, 88 CHKG, $1.80M, expiring) from PHX; Sutton (76 ovr, 94 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 27, $1.34M, 4yr) from ATL
recommendations.summary: Execute the three-deal package agreed 22 December before March: net payroll drops $2.56M, toughness goes from 73 to 91/94, faceoffs gain Sillinger at 91.
recommendations.rationale: STL at 8-23-3 get a 95-overall scorer who still produced 51 points; PHX at 15-21-4 shed $1.80M for a pick with seven expiring deals; ATL at 8-18-2 get a 23-year-old POTE-91 defender plus a fifth-rounder. All three are under .500 and selling.

recommendations.proposed: Draft pick (target: late first or second from a contender needing a playoff backup goalie)
recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour for a draft pick before March via the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic; Aebischer takes the crease.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour's $6.50M is dead money after July. The mechanic converts any 80+ expiring player into a pick. A contender gets a 91-overall goalie for a playoff rental at zero future commitment. Acceptance is uncertain because we cannot identify which specific club has the backup hole.

recommendations.current: Own 1st-round pick + Koltsov (74 ovr, 23, $1.10M, 2yr, POTE 94, surplus per coach)
recommendations.proposed: Doan (84 ovr, 88 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 28, $2.40M, 1yr, 38 pts/41 GP) from PHX
recommendations.summary: Spend the own first-rounder plus Koltsov on Doan: the only 28-year-old in the league who fills toughness and checking simultaneously while remaining a re-sign candidate.
recommendations.rationale: PHX at 15-21-4, $47.81M payroll, $15.08M profit are sellers with seven expiring deals. Doan at one year and $2.40M is a sellable asset. Koltsov at 23 with POTE 94 and two years of control is a rebuild piece. The risk is Doan walking in July after we've surrendered the first; at $2.40M a 3-4 year re-sign is affordable on $27.14M profit.

recommendations.summary: Chara (84 ovr, 92 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 27, $1.7M, 1yr) is the only target that fills toughness AND checking simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Zero players above 73 TOUG on the roster; Chara at 92 is a full 19 points above the best internal option. Ottawa are rebuilding with 11 expiring contracts. Package: first-round pick plus Holden (who at 71 FACE is surplus here).

recommendations.summary: Avery (77 ovr, 94 FACE, 88 TOUG, $0.40M, 2yr) fills faceoffs and toughness in one asset at a late-round-pick price.
recommendations.rationale: Faceoffs has one player at 80+ (Sundin 90); toughness has zero at 80+. Avery is the only available player who addresses both simultaneously. LA at 9-16-5 with 13 expiring deals has no reason to keep a fourth-line centre.

recommendations.summary: Line Tucker on the third unit; he is the sixth-best checker at 83 and is currently unlined.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker's 83 CHKG is the highest unused checking grade on the roster. Koltsov is surplus per coach and carries 92 speed but no role need. The coach already requested this.

recommendations.summary: Restore Spezza to 12+ MPG for a sustained run; he is producing at 0.62 pts/g on 6.2 minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza is the developmental answer at centre while Sundin (33) fades. Coach requests this; the numbers support it. Not a gap-filler but a trajectory requirement.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Aebischer on 2-3 years now; plan to trade Belfour for a pick before March.
recommendations.rationale: Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV, 15-3 in 19 GP) is ready. Belfour at 39, $6.50M, expiring qualifies for the above-80 expiring-asset trade mechanic. Tellqvist (4.11 GAA, 0.865 SV) cannot be the backup.

recommendations.summary: Scoring, playmaking, speed, clutch, and stamina are all covered at 8+ players each above 80.
recommendations.rationale: Even losing Mogilny (35, expiring) leaves Sundin 92, Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90, Salo 88, Roberts 88 in scoring. No acquisition needed here.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik, Richards and Nash to 5-6 year extensions immediately, before July.
recommendations.rationale: They are 22, 24 and 20 with 59, 45 and 30 points on $1.10M/$1.00M/$1.20M deals, and all three sit in the 17-contract, $28.60M cluster expiring this July.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup to 5-6 years before a full season reprices him.
recommendations.rationale: He is 18, $2.34M, two years left, POTE 95, 22 points in 29 games; the rookie-window price disappears after one more top-nine year.
